Ethical guidelines

Authors are expected to meet our ethical guidelines on intellectual property, plagiarism, contributorship, and disclosure of financial support. See the full policies for authors here.

Originality

Submission of a manuscript acknowledges that the manuscript is original and is not, in whole or in part, published or under consideration for publication elsewhere. Authors are also required to attest that the manuscript will not be submitted elsewhere while under consideration for publication in this journal. The submitted article must not be a revision of a rejected article previously submitted to this journal, unless the authors have been explicitly invited to resubmit by the editorial board of the journal.

Use of AI

Authors of papers submitted to this journal may use AI tools for light editing, such as spell-checking and help with grammar, without acknowledgment. Any use of AI in aid of the arguments in a paper or the citations in a paper must be acknowledged. Papers largely created by AI may not be submitted to this journal.

Choice of editor

During submission, authors will be asked to suggest one or more suitable editors to initially handle their submission. They should choose the editor whose interests are closest to the subject of the paper, but who is not directly connected to one of the authors (e.g., as a former advisor/student, a close relative, a colleague at the same institution, or a close collaborator). Sometimes after submission the manuscript is reassigned to another editor for handling.

Language

Articles in GT are usually in English, but articles written in other languages will be considered, provided a relevant editor is comfortable with the language.

Format

Submission requires uploading the paper in PDF format here. If your submission is accepted you will then need to supply source files, preferably in a variety of TeX or LaTeX, or in other software such as Word.

Please follow our LaTeX instructions for authors. Please do not use the public class file gtpart.cls, which is out of date. Use whichever class file you prefer (article.cls, amsart.cls, etc.), and we will convert this in production.

Required items

Abstract

A brief abstract of about 150 words or fewer must be included. It should be self-contained and not make any reference to the bibliography. If the article is not in English, two versions of the abstract must be included, one in the language of the article and one in English.

Keywords and subject codes

Keywords and at least one Mathematics Subject Classification code for the article are required.

Author information

For each coauthor, postal address and affiliation (if appropriate) are required. Each coauthor must provide a valid email address that belongs only to that person and is not shared with anyone. Changes in email address should be communicated promptly.

References

Bibliographical references should be complete, including article titles and page ranges. All references in the bibliography should be cited in the text. The use of BibTeX is preferred but not required. Tags will be converted to the journal format.

Authors attest that all documents listed in the bibliography have been read and absorbed by at least one author. Their relevance to the submission should be highlighted by a description explicit enough to orient the reader.

Figures

Figures must be of publication quality. After acceptance, you will need to submit the original source files in vector graphics format for all diagrams in your manuscript; vector EPS or vector PDF files are the most useful. Bundle your figure files into a single archive (using zip, tar, rar or other format of your choice) and upload on the link you will be provided at acceptance time. For questions, please write to graphics@msp.org with as many details as you can about how your graphics were generated.

Each figure should be captioned and numbered so that it can float. Small figures can be kept in the text (e.g., "The curve looks like this:").

Preprints

If your paper has previously been deposited on arXiv, we will need its arXiv number at acceptance time. This allows us to deposit the DOI of the published version on the paper's arXiv page.

Proofs

Page proofs will be made available to authors (or to the designated corresponding author) in PDF format. Failure to acknowledge the receipt of proofs or to return corrections within the requested deadline may cause publication to be postponed.

id="about-the-journal-aims-and-scope"><h4>Aims and scope</h4><div><p>Emphasizing contributions that represent significant advances in all areas of <b>pure mathematics</b>, <i>Advances in Mathematics</i> provides research mathematicians with an effective medium for communicating important recent developments in their areas of specialization to colleagues and to scientists in related disciplines.</p><p></p></div></div><div id="about-the-journal-open-archive"><h4>Open Archive</h4><div><p>This journal has an <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/open-access/open-archive">Open Archive</a>. All published items, including research articles, have unrestricted access and will remain permanently free to read and download 48 months after publication. All papers in the Archive are subject to <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/our-business/policies/open-access-licenses/elsevier-user-license">Elsevier's user license</a>. </p></div></div><div id="about-the-journal-peer-review"><h4>Peer review</h4><div><p>This journal follows a <span>single anonymized</span> review process. Your submission will initially be assessed by our editors. If your submission is deemed suitable, it will typically be sent to be reviewed by a minimum of <span>one reviewer</span> for an independent expert assessment of the scientific quality. The decision as to whether your article is accepted or rejected for publication will be made by our editors.<br><br>Read more about <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/reviewer/what-is-peer-review">peer review</a>.</p><p>Our editors are not involved in making decisions about papers which:</p><ul><li><p>they have written themselves.</p></li><li><p>have been written by family members or colleagues.</p></li><li><p>relate to products or services in which they have an interest.</p></li></ul><p>Any such submissions will be subject to the journal's usual procedures and peer review will be handled independently of the editor involved and their research group. Read more about <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/publishing-ethics#2-duties-of-editors">editor duties</a>.</p><p>Authors may submit a formal appeal request to the editorial decision, provided it meets all the requirements and follows the procedure outlined in Elsevier’s <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/editorial-decision-appeals-policy">Appeal Policy</a>. Only one appeal per submission will be considered and the appeal decision will be final.</p></div></div><div id="about-the-journal"><div><h4>Special issues and article collections</h4><p>The peer review process for special issues and article collections follows the same process as outlined above for regular submissions, except, a guest editor may send the submissions out to the reviewers and may recommend a decision to the journal editor. The journal editor oversees the peer review process of all special issues and article collections to ensure the high standards of publishing ethics and responsiveness are respected and is responsible for the final decision regarding acceptance or rejection of articles.</p></div></div><div id="about-the-journal-open-access"><h4>Open access</h4><div><p>We refer you to our <a href="https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/journal/00018708/publish/open-access-options">open access information page</a> to learn about open access options for this journal.</p><p></p></div></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies"><h3>Ethics and policies</h3><div id="ethics-and-policies-ethics-in-publishing"><h4>Ethics in publishing</h4><div><p>Authors must follow ethical guidelines stated in Elsevier's <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/publishing-ethics#4-duties-of-authors">Publishing Ethics Policy</a>.</p></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies-submission-declaration"><h4>Submission declaration</h4><div><p>When authors submit an article to an Elsevier journal it is implied that:</p><ul><li><p>The work described has not been published previously except in the form of a preprint, an abstract, a published lecture, academic thesis or registered report. See our policy on <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies/publishing-ethics#Authors">multiple, redundant or concurrent publication</a>.</p></li><li><p>The article is not under consideration for publication elsewhere.</p></li><li><p>The article's publication is approved by all authors and tacitly or explicitly by the responsible authorities where the work was carried out.</p></li><li><p>If accepted, the article will not be published elsewhere in the same form, in English or in any other language, including electronically, without the written consent of the copyright-holder.</p></li></ul><p>To verify compliance with our journal publishing policies, we may check your manuscript with our screening tools.</p></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies-authorship"><h4>Authorship</h4><div><p>All authors should have made substantial contributions to all of the following: </p><ol><li><p>The conception and design of the study, or acquisition of data, or analysis and interpretation of data</p></li><li><p>Drafting the article or revising it critically for important intellectual content.</p></li><li><p>Final approval of the version to be submitted. </p></li></ol><p>All authors are accountable for all aspects of the work, to ensure that questions related to the accuracy or integrity of any part of the work are appropriately investigated and resolved. </p><h4>Corresponding author<b> </b></h4><p>Authors must appoint a single corresponding author to communicate with the journal during the editorial process. This individual submits the manuscript and all required documentation to the journal, and serves as the primary contact between the journal and the co-authors. It is important that all contact details of the corresponding author are kept up to date throughout the submission and publication process.</p><p>Only the corresponding author’s affiliation will be used to determine eligibility for a publishing agreement, and possible discounts related to it. Affiliations of other co-authors are not relevant for eligibility.</p><h4>Group authorship</h4><p>Group authorship refers to the attribution of an article to a defined and named group of authors whose members have contributed to the work. Examples include research consortia, clinical trial groups, collaborative networks, task forces or working groups, expert panels or consensus groups, and participatory research groups.</p><ul><li><p>Group authorship must be declared on the title page <i>at submission.</i> When available, the submitting author should include the group under “Collaborative Author Groups” in the submission system.</p></li><li><p>A corresponding author who agrees to coordinate all communications on behalf of the group must be designated.</p></li><li><p>The group name will be included in the author list in the published article (e.g., “on behalf of the [Consortium Name]”).</p></li><li><p>All group members associated with the work should be listed in a dedicated section, preferably an appendix.</p></li><li><p>All listed authors must follow the journal’s authorship and authorship change policies.</p></li><li><p>The group must maintain a transparent internal process for determining authorship and resolving disputes. All authorship disputes must be resolved within the group.</p></li></ul><p></p></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies-changes-to-authorship"><h4>Changes to authorship</h4><div><p>The editors of this journal generally will not consider changes to authorship once a manuscript has been submitted. It is important that authors carefully consider the authorship list and order of authors and provide a definitive author list at submission.  <br><br>The policy of this journal around authorship changes:  </p><ul><li><p>All authors must be listed in the manuscript and their details entered into the submission system. Changes can only be made prior to acceptance, and only if approved by the journal editor. This includes additions, deletion, or rearrangement of author names.</p></li><li><p>Requests to change authorship must be made by the corresponding author using the <a href="https://legacyfileshare.elsevier.com/gfa/authorship-change-request-form.pdf">Authorship Change Request form</a>. The corresponding author must provide the reason for the request to the journal editor with written confirmation from all authors, including any authors being added or removed, that they agree with the changes. Requests which do not comply with the instructions outlined in the form will not be considered. </p></li><li><p>This journal does not allow authorship changes after acceptance. This includes additions, deletions, or the rearrangement of author names, including changes to the corresponding author. </p></li><li><p>The review process may be paused while a change in authorship request is being considered. </p></li><li><p>Change requests made by the authors without the <a href="https://legacyfileshare.elsevier.com/gfa/authorship-change-request-form.pdf">Authorship Change Request form</a> or editor approval may result in the rejection of the manuscript, or retraction if the article has already been published.<br></p></li></ul><p></p></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies-declaration-of-competing-interests"><h4>Declaration of competing interests</h4><div><p>All authors must disclose any financial and personal relationships with other people or organizations that could inappropriately influence or bias their work. Examples of potential competing interests include:</p><ul><li><p>Employment</p></li><li><p>Consultancies</p></li><li><p>Stock ownership</p></li><li><p>Honoraria</p></li><li><p>Paid expert testimony</p></li><li><p>Patent applications or registrations</p></li><li><p>Grants or any other funding</p></li><li><p>Affiliation with the journal as an Editor or Advisory Board Member</p></li></ul><p>The <a href="https://declarations.elsevier.com/">declarations tool</a> should always be completed.</p><p>Authors with a journal affiliation to declare should enter the following text under “Other Activities” within the  <a href="https://declarations.elsevier.com/">declarations tool</a> and should inform the journal and publisher prior to completing the submission process: </p><p><i>Given their role as [AUTHOR JOURNAL ROLE TITLE], [AUTHOR NAME] had no involvement in the peer-review of this article and has no access to information regarding its peer-review. Full responsibility for the editorial process for this article was delegated to another journal editor.</i></p><p>Editorial disclosure statements will be included as a footnote and/or in the declaration of competing interest section of the article. </p><p>Authors with no competing interests to declare should select the option "I have nothing to declare".</p><p>The resulting Word document containing your declaration should be uploaded at the "attach/upload files" step in the submission process. It is important that the Word document is saved in the .doc/.docx file format. Author signatures are not required.</p></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies-funding-sources"><h4>Funding sources</h4><div><p>Authors must disclose any funding sources who provided financial support for the conduct of the research and/or preparation of the article. The role of sponsors, if any, should be declared in relation to the study design, collection, analysis and interpretation of data, writing of the report and decision to submit the article for publication. If funding sources had no such involvement this should be stated in your submission.</p><p>List funding sources in this standard way to facilitate compliance to funder's requirements:</p><p><i>Funding: This work was supported by the National Institutes of Health [grant numbers xxxx, yyyy]; the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Seattle, WA [grant number zzzz]; and the United States Institutes of Peace [grant number aaaa].</i></p><p>It is not necessary to include detailed descriptions on the program or type of grants, scholarships and awards. When funding is from a block grant or other resources available to a university, college, or other research institution, submit the name of the institute or organization that provided the funding.</p><p>If no funding has been provided for the research, it is recommended to include the following sentence:</p><p><i>This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.</i></p></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies-declaration-of-generative-ai-use"><h4>Declaration of generative AI use</h4><div><p>Authors must declare the use of generative AI tools in the manuscript preparation process upon submission of the paper.</p><p>Generative AI and AI-assisted technologies (“AI tools”) have been rapidly adopted in research and scholarly publishing, offering significant benefits while requiring clear standards for responsible and transparent use.</p><p>Authors preparing a manuscript for this journal may use AI tools to support them. However, these tools must never be used as a substitute for human critical thinking, expertise and evaluation. AI tools may only be applied with human oversight and control.</p><p>Please read Elsevier’s detailed author policy on the use of AI tools, as stated in Elsevier’s <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/generative-ai-policies-for-journals">generative AI policies for journals</a>.</p><p>Ultimately, authors are responsible and accountable for the contents of their work. This includes accountability for: </p><ul><li><p>Carefully reviewing and verifying the accuracy, comprehensiveness, and impartiality of all AI-generated output (including checking the sources, as AI-generated references can be incorrect or fabricated).</p></li><li><p>Editing and adapting all material thoroughly to ensure the manuscript represents the author’s authentic and original contribution and reflects their own analysis, interpretation, insights and ideas.</p></li><li><p>Ensuring accuracy and originality of any AI generated images and provide appropriate attribution where relevant.</p></li><li><p>Ensuring the use of any tools or sources, AI-based or otherwise, is made clear and transparent to readers. If AI tools have been used, we require a disclosure statement upon submission; please see example below.</p></li><li><p>Ensuring the manuscript is developed in a way that safeguards data privacy, intellectual property and other rights, by checking the terms and conditions of any AI tool that is used. </p></li></ul><p>Finally, authors must not list or cite AI tools as an author or co-author on the manuscript since authorship implies responsibilities and tasks that can only be attributed to, and performed by, humans.</p><p>The use of AI tools in the manuscript preparation process must be declared by adding a statement at the end of the manuscript when the paper is first submitted. The statement will appear in the published work and should be placed in a new section before the references list. An example: </p><p>Title of new section: <i>Declaration of generative AI and AI-assisted technologies in the manuscript preparation process. </i><br>Statement: <i>During the preparation of this work the author(s) used [NAME OF TOOL / SERVICE] in order to [REASON]. After using this tool/service, the author(s) reviewed and edited the content as needed and take(s) full responsibility for the content of the published article.</i> </p><p>The declaration does not apply to the use of basic tools, such as tools used to check grammar, spelling and references. In addition, authors are not required to disclose the use of AI tools or features within specialist disability-related assistive technology, provided these are used solely for accessibility purposes.</p><p>If you have nothing to disclose, you do not need to add a statement. </p><p>Please note: to protect authors’ rights and the confidentiality of their research, this journal does not currently allow academic editors and reviewers to upload an unpublished manuscript into a generative AI tool, as is stated in Elsevier’s <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/generative-ai-policies-for-journals">generative AI policies for journals</a>. However, AI tools may be used in a supportive capacity by editors and reviewers to improve structure and language of the review report or editorial decision letter or to conduct a background literature search. Elsevier is actively evaluating compliant AI tools and may revise this policy in the future.</p></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies-preprints"><h4>Preprints</h4><div id="ethics-and-policies-preprints-preprint-sharing"><h5>Preprint sharing</h5><div><p>Authors may share preprints in line with Elsevier's <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies/sharing">article sharing policy</a>. Sharing preprints, such as on a preprint server, will not count as prior publication.</p><p>We advise you to read our policy on <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/publishing-ethics#4-duties-of-authors">multiple, redundant or concurrent publication</a>.</p></div></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies-use-of-inclusive-language"><h4>Use of inclusive language</h4><div><p>Inclusive language acknowledges diversity, conveys respect to all people, is sensitive to differences, and promotes equal opportunities. Authors should ensure their work uses inclusive language throughout and contains nothing which might imply one individual is superior to another on the grounds of:</p><ul><li><p>age</p></li><li><p>gender</p></li><li><p>race</p></li><li><p>ethnicity</p></li><li><p>culture</p></li><li><p>sexual orientation</p></li><li><p>disability or health condition</p></li></ul><p>We recommend avoiding the use of descriptors about personal attributes unless they are relevant and valid. Write for<b> </b>gender neutrality with the use of plural nouns ("clinicians, patients/clients") as default. Wherever possible, avoid using "he, she," or "he/she."</p><p>No assumptions should be made about the beliefs of readers and writing should be free from bias, stereotypes, slang, reference to dominant culture and/or cultural assumptions.</p><p>These guidelines are meant as a point of reference to help you identify appropriate language but are by no means exhaustive or definitive.</p></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies-reporting-sex-and-gender-based-analyses"><h4>Reporting sex- and gender-based analyses</h4><div><p>There is no single, universally agreed-upon set of guidelines for defining sex and gender. We offer the following guidance:</p><ul><li><p>Sex and gender-based analyses (SGBA) should be integrated into research design when research involves or pertains to humans, animals or eukaryotic cells. This should be done in accordance with any requirements set by funders or sponsors and best practices within a field.</p></li><li><p>Sex and/or gender dimensions of the research should be addressed within the article or declared as a limitation to the generalizability of the research.</p></li><li><p>Definitions of sex and/or gender applied should be explicitly stated to enhance the precision, rigor and reproducibility of the research and to avoid ambiguity or conflation of terms and the constructs to which they refer.</p></li></ul><p>We advise you to read the <a href="https://researchintegrityjournal.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s41073-016-0007-6/tables/1">Sex and Gender Equity in Research (SAGER) guidelines</a> and the <a href="https://ease.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/EASE-SAGER-Checklist-2022.pdf">SAGER checklist</a> (PDF) on the EASE website, which offer systematic approaches to the use of sex and gender information in study design, data analysis, outcome reporting and research interpretation.</p><p>For further information we suggest reading the rationale behind and recommended<a href="https://doi.org/10.1186/s41073-016-0007-6"> use of the SAGER guidelines</a>.</p><h5>Definitions of sex and/or gender</h5><p>We ask authors to define how sex and gender have been used in their research and publication. Some guidance:</p><ul><li><p>Sex generally refers to a set of biological attributes that are associated with physical and physiological features such as chromosomal genotype, hormonal levels, internal and external anatomy. A binary sex categorization (male/female) is usually designated at birth ("sex assigned at birth") and is in most cases based solely on the visible external anatomy of a newborn. In reality, sex categorizations include people who are intersex/have differences of sex development (DSD).</p></li><li><p>Gender generally refers to socially constructed roles, behaviors and identities of women, men and gender-diverse people that occur in a historical and cultural context and may vary across societies and over time. Gender influences how people view themselves and each other, how they behave and interact and how power is distributed in society.</p></li></ul><p>Depending on the focus of a paper, sex and/or gender may or may not be relevant to the content of the paper. We recognize that beliefs, attitudes, and laws relating to sex and gender may vary. These articles do not attempt to dictate author beliefs but rather require that, where relevant to an author’s research or paper, the author must provide clear explanations of how the paper and research define and use sex and gender.</p></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies-image-manipulation"><h4>Image manipulation</h4><div><p>We accept that authors sometimes need to adjust images for clarity but any manipulation of images for the purpose of deception or fraud will be seen as scientific ethical abuse and will be dealt with accordingly.</p><p>Authors must adhere to this journal’s policy for graphical images:</p><ul><li><p>No specific feature within an image may be enhanced, obscured, moved, removed or introduced.</p></li><li><p>Adjustments of brightness, contrast, or color balance are acceptable if, and only as long as, they do not obscure or eliminate any information present in the original image.</p></li><li><p>Nonlinear adjustments such as changes to gamma settings must be disclosed in the figure legend.</p></li><li><p>Use of AI tools to create or manipulate primary research images is not permitted. This includes images that represent experimental or observational data, such as western blots, microscopy images, histology images, or patient images. Please read our policy on the use of AI tools in figures, images and artwork, which can be found in Elsevier’s <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/generative-ai-policies-for-journals">GenAI Policies for Journals</a>.</p></li></ul><p>To verify compliance with the above, this journal may send your images to a secure third-party tool to enable screening for image irregularities. Our editors may ask you to provide original data or images if any questions arise as a result of the screening. The final decision as to whether images are acceptable will be taken by our editors.</p><p>Authors are encouraged to carefully check all images before submission and to connect all the data in any figures to the original, unprocessed data.</p></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies-jurisdictional-claims"><h4>Jurisdictional claims</h4><div><p>Elsevier respects the decisions taken by its authors as to how they choose to designate territories and identify their affiliations in their published content. Elsevier’s policy is to take a neutral position with respect to territorial disputes or jurisdictional claims, including, but not limited to, maps and institutional affiliations. For journals that Elsevier publishes on behalf of a third party owner, the owner may set its own policy on these issues. </p><ul><li><p>
Maps: Readers should be able to locate any study areas shown within maps using common mapping platforms. Maps should only show the area actually studied and authors should not include a location map which displays a larger area than the bounding box of the study area. Authors should add a note clearly stating that "<i>map lines delineate study areas and do not necessarily depict accepted national boundaries</i>”.  During the review process, Elsevier’s editors may request authors to change maps if these guidelines are not followed. 
</p></li><li><p>Institutional affiliations: Authors should use either the full, standard title of their institution or the standard abbreviation of the institutional name so that the institutional name can be independently verified for research integrity purposes.
<br></p></li></ul><p></p></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies-delayed-publication"><h4>Delayed publication</h4><div><p>If you need to delay the publication of your article for any reason, please contact the editorial office of the journal or our <a href="https://service.elsevier.com/app/home/supporthub/publishing">Journal Article Publishing Support Center</a> at the earliest possible opportunity. While we will try to ensure that your article is not published before a certain date if you make your request on a timely basis, we cannot guarantee this. Please also note that once the agreed period of delay has expired the article may be published at any time thereafter.</p></div></div><div id="ethics-and-policies-withdrawal-correction-or-retraction"><h4>Withdrawal, correction, or retraction</h4><div><p>For questions about article withdrawal, correction, or retraction, please consult Elsevier’s <a href="https://www-staging.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/article-withdrawal#0-policy-overview">Article Correction, Retraction and Removal Policy</a>. </p></div></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting"><h3>Writing and formatting</h3><div id="writing-and-formatting-file-format"><h4>File format</h4><div><p>We ask you to provide editable source files for your entire submission (including figures, tables and text graphics). Some guidelines:</p><ul><li><p>Save files in an editable format, using the extension .doc/.docx for Word files and .tex for LaTeX files. A PDF is not an acceptable source file.</p></li><li><p>Format Word files in a single-column layout. Double-column formatting is only permitted for LaTeX submissions. </p></li><li><p>Remove any strikethrough and underlined text from your manuscript, unless it has scientific significance related to your article.</p></li><li><p>Use spell-check and grammar-check functions to avoid errors.</p></li></ul><p>We advise you to read our <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/researcher/author/submit-your-paper">Step-by-step guide to publishing with Elsevier</a>.</p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-latex"><h4>LaTeX</h4><div><p>We encourage you use our <a href="https://assets.ctfassets.net/o78em1y1w4i4/5uFmLZJTPDMAUjFnHRpjj8/6f19a979146eb93263763d87a894ab0d/els-cas-templates.zip">LaTeX template</a> when preparing a LaTeX submission. You will be asked to provide all relevant editable source files upon submission or revision.</p><p>Support for your LaTeX submission:</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.elsevier.com/latex">LaTeX submission instructions and templates</a></p></li><li><p>Journal Article Publishing Support Center <a href="https://service.elsevier.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/36917/supporthub/publishing/kw/latex/">LaTeX FAQs and support</a></p></li><li><p>Researcher Academy’s <a href="https://researcheracademy.elsevier.com/writing-research/technical-writing-skills/beginners-guide-writing-manuscript-latex">Beginners’ guide to writing a manuscript in LaTeX</a></p></li></ul><p></p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-title-page"><h4>Title page</h4><div><p>You are required to include the following details on the title page:</p><ul><li><p>Article title. Article titles should be concise and informative. Please avoid abbreviations and formulae, where possible, unless they are established and widely understood, e.g. DNA.</p></li><li><p>Author names. Provide the given name(s) and family name(s) of each author. The order of authors should match the order in the submission system. Carefully check that all names are accurately spelled. You may add your name between parentheses in your own script after the English transliteration.</p></li><li><p>Affiliations, referring to where the work was carried out, below the author names. Indicate affiliations using a lower-case superscript letter immediately after the author's name and in front of the corresponding address. Ensure that you provide the full name and postal address of each affiliation, including the country name.</p></li><li><p>Corresponding author.<i> </i>Clearly indicate who will handle correspondence for your article at all stages of the refereeing and publication process and also post-publication. This responsibility includes answering any future queries about your results, data, or methodology. The email address of the corresponding author must be included on the title page and will be published in the article.</p></li><li><p>Present/permanent address.<i> </i>If an author has changed affiliation since the work described in your article was carried out, or was visiting during that time, a "present address" (or "permanent address") can be indicated by a footnote to the author's name. The address where the author carried out the work must be retained as their main affiliation address. Use superscript Arabic numerals for such footnotes.</p></li></ul><p></p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-abstract"><h4>Abstract</h4><div><p>You are required to provide a concise and factual abstract which does not exceed <span>250</span> words. The abstract should:</p><ul><li><p>State the purpose of your paper.</p></li><li><p>Outline basic procedures followed.</p></li><li><p>Include your main findings, their statistical significance, where applicable, and your principal conclusions.</p></li><li><p>Emphasize new and important aspects of your study or observations.</p></li></ul><p>Some guidelines: </p><ul><li><p>Abstracts must be able to stand alone, as abstracts are often presented separately from the article. </p></li><li><p>Avoid references. If any are essential to include, ensure that you cite the author(s) and year(s). </p></li><li><p>Avoid non-standard or uncommon abbreviations. If any are essential to include, ensure they are defined within your abstract at first mention. </p></li></ul><p></p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-keywords"><h4>Keywords</h4><div><p>You are required to provide <span>1</span> to <span>7</span> keywords for indexing purposes. Keywords should be written in English. Please try to avoid keywords consisting of multiple words (using "and" or "of").</p><p>We recommend that you only use abbreviations in keywords if they are firmly established in the field.</p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-highlights"><h4>Highlights</h4><div><p>You are <span>encouraged</span> to provide article highlights at submission.</p><p>Highlights are a short collection of bullet points that should capture the novel results of your research as well as any new methods used during your study. Highlights will help increase the discoverability of your article via search engines. Some guidelines:</p><ul><li><p>Submit highlights as a separate editable file in the online submission system with the word "highlights" included in the file name.</p></li><li><p>Highlights should consist of 3 to 5 bullet points, each a maximum of 85 characters, including spaces.</p></li></ul><p>We encourage you to view example <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/researcher/author/tools-and-resources/highlights">article highlights</a> and read about the benefits of their inclusion.</p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-tables"><h4>Tables</h4><div><p>Tables must be submitted as editable text, not as images. Some guidelines:</p><ul><li><p>Place tables next to the relevant text or on a separate page(s) at the end of your article.</p></li><li><p>Cite all tables in the manuscript text.</p></li><li><p>Number tables consecutively according to their appearance in the text.</p></li><li><p>Please provide captions along with the tables.</p></li><li><p>Place any table notes below the table body.</p></li><li><p>Avoid vertical rules and shading within table cells.</p></li></ul><p>We recommend that you use tables sparingly, ensuring that any data presented in tables is not duplicating results described elsewhere in the article.</p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-figures-images-and-other-artwork"><h4>Figures, images and other artwork</h4><div><p>Figures, images, diagrams and other graphical media (artwork) must be supplied as separate files along with the manuscript, in line with these <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/author/artwork-and-media-instructions">artwork and media instructions</a>. Some excerpts:</p><p>When submitting artwork:</p><ul><li><p>Cite all images in the manuscript text.</p></li><li><p>Number images according to the order they appear within your article.</p></li><li><p>Submit each image as a separate file using a logical naming convention for your files (for example, Figure_1, Figure_2 etc).</p></li><li><p>Text graphics may be embedded in the text at the appropriate position. If you are working with LaTeX, text graphics may also be embedded in the file.</p></li></ul><h4>Captions</h4><p>All artwork must have a caption. A caption should consist of a brief title (not displayed on the figure itself) and a description of the image. Keep the amount of text to a minimum, though any symbol or abbreviation should be explained.</p><p>Read how to add captions to your submission <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/author/artwork-and-media-instructions/artwork-faq">here</a>.</p><h4>Formats</h4><p>Submit your artwork in the formats listed below, following the given requirements:</p><table><tbody><tr><th><p>Image type</p></th><th><p>Recommended file type</p></th><th><p>Requirements</p></th></tr><tr><td><p>Vector drawings</p></td><td><p>EPS, PDF</p></td><td><p>Embed the font or save text as graphics</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>Photographs (color or grayscale) </p></td><td><p>TIFF, JPG, PNG</p></td><td><p>Minimum resolution 300 dpi (min. width: single column: 1063 pixels; full page: 2244 pixels)</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>Bitmapped line drawings</p></td><td><p>TIFF, JPG, PNG</p></td><td><p>Minimum resolution 1000 dpi (min. width: single column: 3543 pixels; full page: 7480 pixels)</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>Charts and large or shaded tables</p></td><td><p>XLS, XLSX</p></td><td><p>Supply in a clearly readable format</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>Annotated images</p></td><td><p>PPT, PPTX</p></td><td><p>Annotations and text must be legible; Minimum resolution of embedded images 300 dpi</p></td></tr></tbody></table><p>Do not submit:</p><ul><li><p>Files that are too low in resolution.</p></li><li><p>Artwork where text is disproportionately small compared to the image size, as text may become unreadable.</p></li><li><p>Multiple images or graphs combined into one file, as this affects legibility and accessibility. An exception may be made for images that are intended to be compared to each other, such as before, during, and after photographs.</p></li></ul><h4>Color artwork</h4><p>If you submit usable color figures with your accepted article, we will ensure that they appear in color online. Please ensure that color images are accessible to all, including those with impaired color vision. Learn more about <a href="https://www.w3.org/WAI/perspective-videos/contrast/">color and web accessibility</a>.</p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting"><div><p>For articles appearing in print, you will be sent information on costs to reproduce color in the printed version, after your accepted article has been sent to production. At that stage you can indicate if your preference is to have color only in the online version of your article or also in the printed version.</p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-generative-ai-and-figures-images-and-other-artwork"><h4>Generative AI and figures, images and other artwork</h4><div><p>Please read our policy on the use of generative AI and AI-assisted tools in figures, images and artwork, which can be found in Elsevier’s <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/generative-ai-policies-for-journals"><u>GenAI Policies for Journals</u></a>. This policy states:</p><ul><li><p>AI tools may be used to support the creation of explanatory images (such as flow charts, conceptual diagrams, or schematic illustrations)</p></li><li><p>AI tools may be used to create data visualizations (such as plots, charts, graphs, or heatmaps) when the output is directly derived from underlying data using reproducible analytical, computational, or statistical methods.</p></li><li><p>AI tools must not be used to create or alter images that represent primary observed or experimental data (such as western blots, microscopy images, histology images, or patient images) that were not directly obtained in the research. This includes adjustments to brightness, contrast, or color balance, which should only be done using established image processing software.</p></li><li><p>This policy does not prevent the use of AI tools in formal research design or research methods (such as in AI-assisted imaging approaches used for collection and/or interpretation of the underlying research data or predictive modelling of clinical outcomes based on patient data).</p></li></ul><p>Authors are responsible for ensuring the accuracy and originality of all images submitted for publication. If you used generative AI tools to create images in your manuscript, you should disclose this in each image caption as well as in the general Generative AI disclosure statement.</p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-supplementary-material"><h4>Supplementary material</h4><div><p>We encourage the use of supplementary materials such as applications, images and sound clips to enhance research. Some guidelines:</p><ul><li><p>Supplementary material should be accurate and relevant to the research.</p></li><li><p>Cite all supplementary files in the manuscript text.</p></li><li><p>Submit all supplementary materials at the same time as your manuscript. </p></li><li><p>Include a concise, descriptive caption for each supplementary file, describing its content. </p></li><li><p>After submission supplementary files can only be added or replaced in the revision stage of the editorial process.</p></li><li><p>Be aware that all supplementary materials provided will appear online in the exact same way as received. These files will not be checked, formatted or typeset by the production team. </p></li></ul><p></p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-video"><h4>Video</h4><div><p>This journal accepts video material and animation sequences to support and enhance your scientific research. We encourage you to include links to video or animation files within articles. Some guidelines:</p><ul><li><p>When including video or animation file links within your article, refer to the video or animation content by adding a note in your text where the file should be placed.</p></li><li><p>Clearly label files ensuring the given file name is directly related to the file content.</p></li><li><p>Provide files in one of our <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/researcher/author/policies-and-guidelines/artwork-and-media-instructions/media-specifications">recommended file formats</a>. Files should be within our preferred maximum file size of 150 MB per file, 1 GB in total.</p></li><li><p>Provide "stills" for each of your files. These will be used as standard icons to personalize the link to your video data. You can choose any frame from your video or animation or make a separate image.</p></li><li><p>Provide descriptive text in your manuscript to refer to the video content. This text helps ensure accessibility for visually impaired readers who rely on descriptive information. For journals publishing in print this is also essential, as video and animation files cannot be embedded in the print version. </p></li></ul><p>We publish all video and animation files supplied in the electronic version of your article.</p><p>For more detailed instructions, we recommend that you read our guidelines on <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/researcher/author/policies-and-guidelines/artwork-and-media-instructions/media-overview">submitting video content to be included in the body of an article</a>.</p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-research-data"><h4>Research data</h4><div id="writing-and-formatting-research-data"><div><p>We are committed to supporting the storage of, access to and discovery of research data, and our <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/research-data">research data policy</a> sets out the principles guiding how we work with the research community to support a more efficient and transparent research process.</p><p>Research data refers to the results of observations or experimentation that validate research findings, which may also include software, code, models, algorithms, protocols, methods and other useful materials related to the project.</p><p>Please read our guidelines on <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/researcher/author/tools-and-resources/research-data">sharing research data</a> for more information on depositing, sharing and using research data and other relevant research materials.</p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-research-data"><div><p><b>Research data deposit and citation<br><br></b>For this journal, <b>Option A</b> instructions from our <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/researcher/author/tools-and-resources/research-data/data-guidelines">research data guidelines</a> apply. This means that you are <b>encouraged </b>to:</p><ul><li><p>Deposit your research data in a relevant data repository.</p></li><li><p>Cite this dataset in your article.</p></li></ul><p></p></div></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-data-linking"><h4>Data linking</h4><div><p>Linking to the data underlying your work increases your exposure and may lead to new collaborations. It also provides readers with a better understanding of the described research.</p><p>If your research data has been made available in a data repository there are a number of ways your article can be linked directly to the dataset:</p><ul><li><p>Provide a link to your dataset when prompted during the online submission process.</p></li><li><p>For some data repositories, a repository banner will automatically appear next to your published article on ScienceDirect.</p></li><li><p>You can also link relevant data or entities within the text of your article through the use of identifiers. Use the following format: Database: 12345 (e.g. TAIR: AT1G01020; CCDC: 734053; PDB: 1XFN).</p></li></ul><p>Learn more about <a href="https://www.elsevier.com/researcher/author/tools-and-resources/research-data/data-base-linking">linking research data and research articles in ScienceDirect</a>.</p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-article-structure"><h4>Article structure</h4><div id="writing-and-formatting-article-structure-article-sections"><h5>Article sections</h5><div><p>Divide your manuscript into clearly defined sections covering all essential elements using headings.</p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-article-structure-acknowledgements"><h5>Acknowledgements</h5><div><p>Include any individuals who provided you with help during your research, such as help with language, writing or proof reading, in the acknowledgements section.</p><p>Acknowledgements should be placed in a separate section which appears directly before the reference list. Do not include acknowledgements on your title page, as a footnote to your title, or anywhere else in your article other than in the separate acknowledgements section. </p><p></p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-article-structure-appendices"><h5>Appendices</h5><div><p>We ask you to use the following format for appendices:</p><ul><li><p>Identify individual appendices within your article using the format: A, B, etc.</p></li><li><p>Give separate numbering to formulae and equations within appendices using formats such as Eq. (A.1), Eq. (A.2), etc. and in subsequent appendices, Eq. (B.1), Eq. (B. 2) etc. In a similar way, give separate numbering to tables and figures using formats such as Table A.1; Fig. A.1, etc.</p></li></ul><p></p></div></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-references"><h4>References</h4><div id="writing-and-formatting-references-references-within-text"><h5>References within text</h5><div><p>Any references cited in your article should also be present in your reference list and vice versa. Some guidelines: </p><ul><li><p>References cited in your abstract must be given in full.</p></li><li><p>Make sure all data provided in your reference list are correct and complete.</p></li><li><p>Every reference included must correspond to a real, existing source. </p></li><li><p>Where available include Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs), as they provide a permanent link to the electronic article referenced and improve the discoverability of your research.</p></li><li><p>We recommend not including unpublished results and personal communications in your reference list, though you may mention them in the text of your article. If included, they must follow the standard reference style of the journal, substituting the publication date with “unpublished results” or “personal communication”.</p></li><li><p>References cited as “in press” imply that the item has been accepted for publication. </p></li></ul><p></p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-references-reference-format"><h5>Reference format</h5><div><p>This journal does not set strict requirements on reference formatting at submission. Some guidelines:</p><ul><li><p>References can be in any style or format as long as the style is consistent.</p></li><li><p>Author names, journal or book titles, chapter or article titles, year of publication, volume numbers, article numbers or pagination must be included, where applicable.</p></li></ul><p>Our journal reference style will be applied to your article after acceptance, at proof stage. If required, at this stage we will ask you to correct or supply any missing reference data.</p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-references-reference-style"><h5>Reference style</h5><div><p>Indicate references by adding a number within square brackets in the text. You can refer to author names within your text, but you must always give the reference number, e.g., "as demonstrated [3,6]. Barnaby and Jones [8] obtained a different result ....".</p><p>The list of references should be arranged alphabetically and then numbered (numbers in square brackets).</p><p>Abbreviate journal names according to the <a href="https://portal.issn.org/ltwa">List of Title Word Abbreviations</a> (LTWA).</p><p>Examples:</p><h5>Reference to a journal publication:</h5><p>[1] J. van der Geer, T. Handgraaf, R.A. Lupton, The art of writing a scientific article, J. Sci. Commun. 163 (2020) 51 – 59. <u>https://doi.org/10.1016/j.sc.2020.00372</u>.</p><h5>Reference to a journal publication with an article number:</h5><p>[2] J. van der Geer, T. Handgraaf, R.A. Lupton, 2022. The art of writing a scientific article. Heliyon. 19, e00205. <u>https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heliyon.2022.e00205</u>.</p><h5>Reference to a book:</h5><p>[3] W. Strunk Jr., E.B. White, The Elements of Style, fourth ed., Longman, New York, 2000.</p><h5>Reference to a chapter in a book:</h5><p>[4] G.R. Mettam, L.B. Adams, How to prepare an electronic version of your article, in: B.S. Jones, R.Z. Smith (Eds.), Introduction to the Electronic Age, E-Publishing Inc., New York, 2020, pp. 281 – 304.</p><h5>Reference to a website:</h5><p>[5] Cancer Research UK, Cancer statistics reports for the UK. <u>http://www.cancerresearchuk.org/aboutcancer/statistics/cancerstatsreport/</u>, 2023 (accessed 13 March 2023).</p><h5>Reference to a dataset:</h5><p>[6] M. Oguro, S. Imahiro, S. Saito, T. Nakashizuka,Mortality data for Japanese oak wilt disease and surrounding forest compositions [dataset], Mendeley Data, v1, 2015. <u>https://doi.org/10.17632/xwj98nb39r.1</u>.</p><h5>Reference to software:</h5><p>[7] E. Coon, M. Berndt, A. Jan, D. Svyatsky, A. Atchley, E. Kikinzon, D. Harp, G. Manzini, E. Shelef, K. Lipnikov, R. Garimella, C. Xu, D. Moulton, S. Karra, S. Painter, E. Jafarov, S. Molins, Advanced Terrestrial Simulator (ATS) v0.88 [software], Zenodo, March 25, 2020. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3727209.</p></div></div><div id="writing-and-formatting-references-web-references"><h5>Web references</h5><div><p>When listing web references, as a minimum you should provide the full URL and the date when the reference was last accessed. <h2><a data-link-id="c79871ea-e6cb-4fc1-a94e-919305db8a4e" id="Publication Ethics" name="Publication Ethics"></a>Publication Ethics</h2>

<h3>Publication Ethics and Malpractice Statement</h3>

<p><em>EHJ</em> and Oxford University Press are members of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE), and follows the <a data-link-id="de57596d-46eb-4bd5-b808-68d176a05d91" href="https://publicationethics.org/guidance">guidance provided by COPE</a>. The Journal also subscribes to the ICMJE <a data-link-id="ff886413-0cad-43e8-bb6f-a0fbc068c6d1" href="https://www.icmje.org/recommendations/">Recommendations for the Conduct, Reporting, Editing and Publication of Scholarly work in Medical Journals</a>. It is expected that all parties involved in the publication of content in <em>EHJ</em> (the publisher, editors, authors, and reviewers) follow these guidelines on best practice and publication ethics. The Journal is committed to investigating cases of alleged editor, author, and reviewer misconduct arising from its activities, and will follow COPE Guidelines in all cases.</p>

<p>The Editors are further supported by the ESC Journal Publication Ethics Committee.</p>

<p></p><p>Manuscripts may also be screened, including with services provided by third parties, to help detect integrity issues such as inappropriate image alteration and papermill activity.</p>
<p></p>

<h3><a data-link-id="fd84fd5f-1c7b-4e59-be17-bb316d0a6186" id="Authorship" name="Authorship"></a>Authorship</h3>

<p>All individuals listed as authors should qualify for authorship and should have participated sufficiently in the work to take public responsibility for appropriate portions of the content. Each author included in the manuscript must meet ALL of the following conditions, as specified in the guidelines of the ICMJE. To qualify as an author, the individual must have</p>

<ol>
	<li>made substantial contributions to the conception or design of the work; or the acquisition, analysis, or interpretation of data for the work; AND;</li>
	<li>drafted the work or reviewed it critically for important intellectual content; AND;</li>
	<li>given final approval of the version to be published AND;</li>
	<li>agreed to be accountable for all aspects of the work in ensuring that questions related to the accuracy or integrity of any part of the work are appropriately investigated and resolved.</li>
</ol>

<p>All individuals who meet the authorship criteria listed above should be listed as authors. Individuals who do not meet the above authorship criteria should not be listed as authors. The Journal considers all forms of ghost authorship, in which an individual contributes in the role of an author (according to the criteria above) but is not listed as an author on the manuscript, and all forms of guest or gift authorship, in which individuals are included though they do not meet the above criteria, as unethical and unacceptable.</p>

<p>The corresponding author is responsible for providing the full list of co-authors on the manuscript. Once the manuscript has been submitted, the co-authors will receive an email asking them to verify their contribution to the manuscript. The corresponding author is responsible for ensuring that this step is completed.</p>

<p>For more information about authorship, see the <a data-link-id="1c6e1523-b2bd-411c-a5f7-9581275cb74b" href="https://www.icmje.org/recommendations/browse/roles-and-responsibilities/defining-the-role-of-authors-and-contributors.html">ICMJE guidelines</a>.</p>

<h4>Author changes</h4>

<p>After manuscript submission, no authorship changes (including the authorship list, author order, and who is designated as the corresponding author) should be made unless there is a substantive reason to do so. The editor and all co-authors must agree on the change(s), and neither the Journal nor the publisher mediates authorship disputes. If individuals cannot agree on the authorship of a submitted manuscript, contact the editorial office at <a data-link-id="783f96a3-2324-422e-a20e-6b920c773455" href="mailto:ehj@gemelli-isola.it">ehj@gemelli-isola.it</a>. The dispute must be resolved among the individuals and their institution(s) before the manuscript can be accepted for publication. If an authorship dispute or change arises after a paper is accepted, contact OUP’s Author Support team at <a data-link-id="80bc9a05-0dea-46d1-92e9-719d6878f002" href="mailto:jnls.author.support@oup.com">jnls.author.support@oup.com</a>. COPE provides <a data-link-id="3d80b13d-fd34-48b3-9192-2498069e1674" href="https://publicationethics.org/guidance/guideline/how-handle-authorship-disputes-guide-new-researchers">guidance for authors on resolving authorship disputes</a>.</p>

<h4>Artificial Intelligence</h4>

<p>Natural language processing tools driven by artificial intelligence (AI) do not qualify as authors, and the Journal will screen for them in author lists. The use of AI (for example, to help generate content or images, write code, process data, or for translation) should be disclosed in a cover letter at the point of submission and explained in full in a Methods or Acknowledgements section in the manuscript. Please see the <a data-link-id="ecb68c13-4b34-4c6c-850e-e7925bbbbe60" href="https://publicationethics.org/guidance/cope-position/authorship-and-ai-tools">COPE position statement on Authorship and AI</a> for more details.</p>

<h4>CRediT</h4>

<p>The Journal uses the contributor roles taxonomy (CRediT), which allows authors to describe the contributor roles in a standardized, transparent, and accurate way. Authors should choose from the contributor roles outlined on the <a data-link-id="1339f072-03bb-40da-8c87-c96ae0e09b13" href="https://credit.niso.org/">CRediT website</a> and supply this information upon submission. You may choose multiple contributor roles per author. Any other individuals who do not meet authorship criteria and made less substantive contributions should be listed in your manuscript as non-author contributors with their contributions clearly described.</p>

<h4><a data-link-id="5c8cdb64-089f-4e22-a609-96223d36ad16" id="Contributors" name="Contributors"></a>Contributors</h4>

<p>Any other individual contributor or group of contributors to the work who do not qualify for authorship but who meet some of the four ICMJE criteria listed above should be listed in the article in a section under the heading “Acknowledgements”. As per the ICMJE guidelines, the contribution of each individual or group must be specified. For more information, refer to <a data-link-id="ca2aea43-bae2-4500-8238-be72df39b12e" href="https://www.icmje.org/recommendations/browse/roles-and-responsibilities/defining-the-role-of-authors-and-contributors.html#three">section 3 of the ICMJE guidelines</a>.</p>

<h4>Group Authorship</h4>

<p>The Journal will consider group author names providing the following conditions are met:</p>

<ul>
	<li>The group author name should be the name of a legitimate group. It cannot be a generic name such as “Reviewers” or “Task force”.</li>
	<li>Individuals in the group must <em>collectively</em> meet the ICMJE requirements for authorship as specified above.</li>
	<li>Individuals in the group must each provide a Conflict of Interest form. Please see the Disclosure of Interest section below.</li>
</ul>

<p><a data-link-id="16564874-7b67-4243-8601-23abcb964384" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Group%20Authorship">Formatting your manuscript if there is a group author</a></p>

<h3><a data-link-id="0362ab78-93e4-4070-89a9-8a2101d9b2d5" id="Disclosure of Interest" name="Disclosure of Interest"></a>Disclosure of Interest</h3>

<p>All authors must declare any conflicts of interest. It is the responsibility of the submitting author to ascertain any conflicts of interest from co-authors and declare these at the point of submission. Any potential conflict of interest that might constitute an embarrassment to any of the authors if it were not to be declared and were to emerge after publication should be declared.</p>

<p><a data-link-id="1db75999-3cdc-41bb-a15d-e0fc0e07390d" href="https://academic.oup.com/journals/pages/authors/preparing_your_manuscript/ethics#conflict">A detailed definition of conflicts of interests</a></p>

<p>Instructions for the corresponding author:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Submit an ICMJE <a data-link-id="48b3afe8-9650-40c3-a634-7c5147a96321" href="https://www.icmje.org/disclosure-of-interest/">disclosure of potential conflicts of interest (COI) form</a> for each author by revision stage at the latest.</li>
	<li>When the form is uploaded to Editorial Manager, include the author’s last name in the document title of the form.</li>
	<li>A form must be submitted even if there are no conflicts of interest to declare, in which case the disclosure of interest form should state “none declared”</li>
	<li>Submit a concise and accurate summary of any conflicts of interest declared in the ICMJE forms in the separate <a data-link-id="38259e37-f1e0-494e-85c7-0efbe214fd77" href="https://static.primary.prod.gcms.the-infra.com/static/site/eurheartj/document/ehj-declarations-form.docx?node=fa062d899ef89b868eb1">Declarations Form</a>, and upload the Declarations form under the “Declarations Form” header. If there are no conflicts of interest, state “Conflict of interest: none declared”.</li>
	<li>Authors that hold a position on the Editorial Board of <em>EHJ </em>in any capacity are required to declare their role in their conflict of interest statement. <a data-link-id="069673cf-76e6-430b-a534-b75e09239318" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Papers%20submitted%20by%20Editors%20of%20EHJ">More information about papers submitted by Editors of <em>EHJ</em></a>.</li>
</ul>

<h3>Plagiarism and Redundant Publication</h3>

<p>COPE defines plagiarism as ‘when somebody presents the work of others (data, words or theories) as if they were his/her own and without proper acknowledgement’.</p>

<p>COPE defines redundant publication as ‘when a published work (or substantial sections from a published work) is/are published more than once (in the same or another language) without adequate acknowledgment of the source/cross-referencing/justification or when the same (or substantially overlapping) data is presented in more than one publication without adequate cross-referencing/justification, particularly when this is done in such a way that reviewers/readers are unlikely to realise that most or all the findings have been published before”.</p>

<p>Manuscripts submitted to <em>EHJ</em> may be screened with iThenticate anti-plagiarism software to detect and prevent plagiarism and redundant publication. Any manuscript may be screened, especially if there is reason to suppose that part or all of the manuscript has been previously published. <h3><a data-link-id="1972ee79-c4fe-4735-b561-8d397afff4ab" id="Re-using Copyrighted Material" name="Re-using Copyrighted Material"></a>Re-using Copyrighted Material</h3>

<p>Authors must obtain permission for any material being reproduced – including quotations, images, tables, or videos – for which they are not the copyright holder. Permissions should be sought from the original copyright holder.</p>

<p>If the manuscript contains material for which the authors do not have open access re-use permissions, the following credit line should be included with the material:</p>

<ul>
	<li><em>Title of content</em></li>
	<li><em>Author, Original publication, year of original publication, by permission of [rights holder]</em></li>
	<li><em>This image/content is not covered by the terms of the Creative Commons licence of this publication. For permission to reuse, please contact the rights holder.</em></li>
</ul>

<p><a data-link-id="bbbad5b1-2b06-47cb-ad59-466b43bf6acf" href="https://academic.oup.com/pages/for-authors/journals/preparing-and-submitting-your-manuscript/rights-and-permissions-for-authors">Further information on obtaining permissions</a></p>

<p>All permissions letters should be included with the original submission via Editorial Manager.</p>

<p>If the manuscript does not contain any reproduced material, authors should upload a word document under the head ‘Permissions’ in Editorial Manager, with the following statement: “The authors hereby declare that all illustrations and figures in the manuscript are original and do not require permission to reuse”.</p>

<h3>Geopolitical considerations</h3>

<p>The Journal remains neutral with regards to geopolitical issues.</p>

<p>When including maps, you should include information on how the map was generated or sourced, and the text should also include any geopolitical considerations.</p>

<p>Maps should be meaningful, informative, and accurate in the context of the research. You may consider including a statement of geopolitical neutrality.</p>

<p>All territorial descriptions, maps, and author affiliations are provided by you; therefore, they do not necessarily represent the views of the editorial team, the European Society of Cardiology, or OUP.</p>

<h2><a data-link-id="87a69f41-c0ba-4cae-98e3-12a78337bbd4" id="Peer Review Process" name="Peer Review Process"></a>Peer Review Process</h2>

<h3><a data-link-id="c780f920-ca97-4737-b1ff-b57bfb7dd9ef" id="Peer Review Policy" name="Peer Review Policy"></a>Peer Review Policy</h3>

<p>The Journal operates single-anonymized peer review, meaning that the identity of the authors is known to the editors and to the reviewers, but that the reviewers’ identities are known only to the editors and are hidden from the authors.</p>

<p>All manuscripts submitted to the Journal will be assessed by the Editorial Board. Some manuscripts will be returned to authors at this stage if they are deemed more appropriate for another ESC Journal, if the paper does not meet submission requirements, or if they are deemed to have insufficient priority for further consideration.</p>

<p>Once a submitted manuscript passes initial assessment, it will then be passed to a handling editor, who will oversee peer review and recommend a final decision. The Editor-in-Chief makes the final decision on the submitted manuscript.</p>

<p>Editors and reviewers must not handle manuscripts if they have a conflict of interest with an author or the content. The Journal makes every effort to avoid potential conflicts of interest in the assignment of other editors and peer reviewers. For more information, please see the section on <a data-link-id="61ba9a68-7027-4c6a-a806-dfd89216241f" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Disclosure%20of%20Interest">Disclosure of potential conflicts of interest</a>. During the peer review phase, your manuscript is typically sent to at least two reviewers. All peer review comments are confidential.</p>

<p>You may suggest potential reviewers at submission. However, there is no guarantee the suggested reviewers will be selected by the Journal. Recommended reviewers should be experts in their field and able to provide an objective assessment of your manuscript without financial or interpersonal conflicts of interest with any authors. We encourage you to consider reviewers from a diverse range of backgrounds, including those from under-represented communities. Authors also have the option to request that specific individuals are not used as reviewers of the manuscript. Please provide a brief explanation as to why you have made the request in your Cover Letter. Please note that there is no guarantee these individuals will be excluded as reviewers.</p>

<p>Statistical methods should be rigorous, and reporting of statistical findings should be accurate and complete. All papers provisionally accepted for publication will undergo a detailed statistical review.</p>

<p>If your manuscript is accepted for publication, no information about the review process or editorial decision process is published, unless one of the authors has a role on the journal. See the Disclosure of potential conflicts of interest section for more information in that case.</p>

<p><em>European Heart Journal</em> has partnered with ORCID Reviewer Deposit. This is a third-party service that seeks to track, verify, and give credit for peer review. Reviewers for <em>European Heart Journal</em> can opt in to claim their reviews or have them automatically verified and added to their reviewer profile. Reviewers claiming credit for their review will be associated with the relevant journal, but the article name, reviewer’s decision, and the content of their review is not published on the site. For more information visit the <a data-link-id="1567dd30-077c-419d-9639-e930db3ac90d" href="https://support.orcid.org/hc/en-us/articles/360006971333-Peer-Reviews">ORCID website</a>.</p>

<h3>Fast Track Status</h3>

<p>Available for: Clinical Research Articles, Translational Science Articles and Meta-analyses</p>

<p>Fast Track status is available for selected articles that, in the view of the Editors, warrant expedited peer review and publication. Reasons may include (but are not limited to):</p>

<ul>
	<li>High relevance of the research to the current time (i.e., topicality)</li>
	<li>Requirement to publish on a specified date (e.g., congresses)</li>
</ul>

<p>Authors aiming to publish their paper simultaneously with a conference should submit as early as possible, ideally at least 4 weeks prior to the event. The Journal will endeavour to process the manuscript as quickly as possible.</p>

<p>Fast Track status does not in any way guarantee acceptance and all manuscripts are subject to the same <a data-link-id="7ce5ef9b-9b0b-4c4f-9d8a-7195500138eb" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Peer%20Review%20Policy">peer review policy</a> as other manuscripts.</p>

<p>Papers that are not selected for Fast Track status can be submitted as a regular manuscript.</p>

<h4>How to apply for Fast Track status</h4>

<p>Authors should submit the following items in Editorial Manager, using the article type ‘Fast Track Petition’:</p>

<ul>
	<li>A cover letter explaining why the manuscript is suitable for Fast Track status</li>
	<li>The text abstract as a separate file</li>
	<li>The manuscript as a separate file</li>
</ul>

<p>A Fast Track petition will not be considered without all items listed above.</p>

<h4>When Fast Track status is offered</h4>

<ol>
	<li>The corresponding author will receive an email to confirm that Fast Track status has been granted.</li>
	<li>The manuscript will be returned to the corresponding author.</li>
	<li>The corresponding author will need to complete the full manuscript submission process.</li>
</ol>

<p>For manuscripts with Fast Track status, the Editorial Office aims to return an initial decision within 7 working days.</p>

<p>The Journal aims to publish the final version of Fast Track articles within 10 working days post-acceptance, pending the timely receipt of the license to publish and proof corrections from the corresponding author.</p>

<p>Fast Track manuscripts intended for simultaneous publication with a presentation at a major international congress will be published as an accepted manuscript (in the form of a non-typeset PDF) once the corresponding author signs the license, while adhering to any embargo restrictions in place. Subsequently, the accepted manuscript will be typeset, and the final version of record will replace the accepted manuscript version online.</p>

<h4>When Fast Track status is not offered</h4>

<ul>
	<li>The corresponding author will receive an email to confirm that Fast Track status has not been granted.</li>
	<li>The manuscript will be returned to the corresponding author.</li>
	<li>The corresponding author can submit the manuscript as a regular manuscript by changing the article type from ‘Fast Track Petition’ to an appropriate article type from the list given in the submission system.</li>
</ul>

<h3>ESC Manuscript Transfer</h3>

<p>Authors submitting to the Journal will be given the opportunity to indicate whether their manuscript can be considered for transfer to another ESC Journal if <em>EHJ</em> is unable to consider the manuscript further. If a transfer decision is reached and the author agrees to the offer, the manuscript files and any reviewer reports from consenting reviewers will be sent to the receiving journal. The Editors at the receiving journal may choose to seek additional peer review. A decision will be made on the manuscript based on the feedback from all reviewers and the judgment of the receiving journal’s Editors.</p>

<p><a data-link-id="a81431d7-cafb-4eb1-8b65-68fdc33551c9" href="https://academic.oup.com/esc/pages/manuscript_sharing">More information about the ESC Manuscript Transfer Service</a></p>

<p>Authors of Cardiovascular Flashlights will be given the opportunity to indicate whether their manuscript could be considered for transfer to <a data-link-id="ad93672d-dcba-4556-aa18-adc5d1ae2bf1" href="https://academic.oup.com/ehjcr"><em>European Heart Journal – Case Reports</em></a> if <em>EHJ</em> is unable to consider their manuscript further.</p>

<h3><a data-link-id="4c16f9e0-cb31-4e60-a50f-3198c8f4c9cf" id="Papers submitted by Editors of EHJ" name="Papers submitted by Editors of EHJ"></a>Papers submitted by Editors of <em>EHJ</em></h3>

<p>To ensure that manuscripts receive unbiased evaluation, it is the Journal’s policy that papers in which an Editor at <em>EHJ</em> is an author or contributor will be assigned to another Editor at <em>EHJ</em> (who is not at the same institute). This Editor will oversee the peer review and decision-making process. This policy also applies to papers where an Editor has declared any other conflict of interest.</p>

<p>Any manuscript in which the Editor-in-Chief is an author or contributor will be assigned to an external Guest Editor. Papers that are handled by a Guest Editor will include a statement at the bottom of the article.</p>

<p>The corresponding author should indicate in the cover letter if an Editor from <em>EHJ</em> is a co-author or contributor to the manuscript.</p>

<p>Individuals that have any conflicts of interest relating to the peer review and decision-making process are excluded from the process.</p>

<h3>Appealing a Decision</h3>

<p>If the authors have reason to believe that the review process or final decision has not been fair or well-informed, the authors may submit an appeal to the Journal. Appeals can be submitted within one month of the final decision on the manuscript. Only one appeal per manuscript will be considered. The appeal will be considered carefully by the Editor-in-Chief and the Editorial Board.</p>

<p>The authors should provide the appeal in a word document and attach it to an email to <a data-link-id="d0c3955e-032d-4643-ac1c-74d58f4b9940" href="mailto:ehj@gemelli-isola.it">ehj@gemelli-isola.it</a>. The appeal should include:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Names of all authors submitting the appeal</li>
	<li>Email addresses and contact details of the authors, or the corresponding author</li>
	<li>Full manuscript title</li>
	<li>Manuscript ID from Editorial Manager</li>
	<li>An explanation outlining why the final decision was unfair or not merited</li>
	<li>Specific comments in relation to the peer review reports</li>
</ul>

<h3>Reporting Demographic Information for Study Participants</h3>

<p>The Journal uses the following definitions, adapted from the definitions that were proposed by the United States National Institutes of Health. Sex and gender are distinct terms and are not interchangeable.</p>

			<th>Term</th>
			<th>Definition</th>
		</tr>
		<tr>

			<td>This term is a biological descriptor that includes anatomy, physiology, genetics and hormones.</td>
		</tr>
		<tr>
			<td>Gender</td>
			<td>This term refers to the cultural and psychosocial construct that varies from society to society and can change over time.</td>
		</tr>

</table></div>

<p>Authors should refer to the <a data-link-id="4baa2c4e-dc6d-45fa-9cb7-fcdb0bc98bd8" href="https://researchintegrityjournal.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s41073-016-0007-6">Sex and Gender Equity in Research (SAGER) guidelines</a> when preparing their manuscript for submission to the Journal.</p>

<p>In your manuscript:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Article titles and abstracts should indicate what sex(es) or gender(s) the study applies to.</li>
	<li>The methods section should report how sex and/or gender was considered in the design of the study.</li>
	<li>The results section should include data stratified by sex and/or gender as appropriate.</li>
	<li>All data should be de-identified.</li>
	<li>If a sex and/or gender analysis was not conducted, the rationale should be provided.</li>
	<li>If space in the main body of the manuscript is limited the above information can be provided as supplementary material.</li>
</ul>

<p><a data-link-id="9d412a70-7014-4967-963a-f38af1b8ea2c" href="https://researchintegrityjournal.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s41073-016-0007-6">Read further guidance on reporting sex and gender information from SAGER</a></p>

Remember that views of race and identity vary from place to place and change over time.</p>
