<h3><a data-link-id="c707e8a1-cbbd-4138-84be-37be38a26e9f" id="Informed Patient Consent" name="Informed Patient Consent"></a>Informed Patient Consent</h3>

<p>Authors should observe high standards with respect to publication ethics as set out by the <a data-link-id="80bd2200-bab2-4bbf-a208-304b4389632b" href="https://publicationethics.org/">Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE)</a> and <a data-link-id="5873953c-c28d-4398-87f0-1fa33c4ccf33" href="https://www.icmje.org/recommendations/browse/roles-and-responsibilities/protection-of-research-participants.html">International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) recommendations for reporting about patients</a>. Patients have a right to privacy that should not be infringed without prior informed consent.</p>

<p>Identifying information should not be published in written descriptions, photographs, or pedigrees unless the information is essential for scientific purposes and the patient (or parent or guardian) has given written informed consent for publication. Informed consent for this purpose requires that the patient be shown the manuscript to be published.</p>

<p>Identifying details should be omitted if they are not essential, but patient data should never be altered or falsified to attain anonymity or to deidentify the data.</p>

<p>The Journal requires at the point of submission that a consent form has been completed for any manuscripts in which an individual or a group of individuals can be identified. A statement addressing informed patient consent must be included as part of the manuscript under the heading “Consent”. If the patient or relatives of a deceased patient cannot be traced and consent cannot be obtained, the case or data can only be considered for publication if it is sufficiently de-identified.</p>

<p>Completed consent forms should not be submitted to the Journal. Completed forms should be held by the treating institution according to locally approved procedures. The consent form should be made available to the Journal if specifically requested.</p>

<p>The Editorial Board reserves the right to reject papers for which the ethical aspects are, in the opinion of the Editorial Board, open to doubt. Authors can contact the Editorial Office with any queries regarding consent.</p>

<h3>Statistics</h3>

<p>The application of adequate statistical methods is required for publication in <em>EHJ</em>. The Journal advises authors to be as simple as possible, but as sophisticated as needed. For example, clinical trials with their formalized framework must meet more specific statistical standards than pathophysiological studies. Authors are advised to include absolute risk as well as relative risk where possible. For studies with a sophisticated design, the collaboration of a professional statistician is recommended.</p>

<p>As part of the review process, the Journal may send the manuscript to a Statistical Reviewer for evaluation.</p>

<p>Authors should refer to the following guidance before submitting:</p>

<ul>
	<li>‘Statistical Analysis’ in the <em>EHJ</em> <a data-link-id="c7ad43cf-9b63-46ba-a34c-c85e15ba4f00" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/article/42/28/2729/6325300">Quality Standards document </a></li>
	<li><a data-link-id="5d9b27c7-eaac-4ff9-8764-ab8c384646d3" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/statistics">A detailed summary of relevant points regarding study design, analysis and reporting </a></li>
</ul>

<h2><a data-link-id="72bafabd-971f-48e0-80dd-b547c0886e00" id="Availability of Data and Materials" name="Availability of Data and Materials"></a>Availability of Data and Materials</h2>

<h3>Data Policy</h3>

<p>Where ethically feasible, the Journal strongly encourages authors to make all deidentified data and software code on which the conclusions of the paper rely available to readers.</p>

<p>The Journal suggests that data is presented in the main manuscript or in additional supporting files, or that authors deposit the data in a public repository. <a data-link-id="d57a076e-bec5-47e6-aa46-fe7d00290b5e" href="https://academic.oup.com/journals/pages/authors/preparing_your_manuscript/research-data-policy#choosing">Information on general repositories for all data types, and a list of recommended repositories by subject area</a></p>

<p>In support of the Journal’s policy, authors are required to include a <a data-link-id="f4790dc9-4c20-4a99-837d-c86f30a4dbaa" href="https://academic.oup.com/journals/pages/authors/preparing_your_manuscript/research-data-policy#data2">Data Availability Statement</a> in their article, even if no data are presented or discussed. These statements help readers to understand the availability of data underlying the research results described in the article. The statement may refer to original data generated in the course of the study or to third-party data analysed in the article. The statement should describe and provide means of access, where possible, by linking to the data or providing the required unique identifier. If no data is presented or discussed in the paper, the following (or similar) should be stated: “No new data were generated or analysed in support of this research”. Authors should provide the data availability statement as part of the <a data-link-id="dbb6f873-6231-41f2-976c-67cbcd81ac57" href="https://static.primary.prod.gcms.the-infra.com/static/site/eurheartj/document/ehj-declarations-form.docx?node=fa062d899ef89b868eb1">Declarations Form</a>.</p>

<p><a data-link-id="13d72234-df1d-4f31-b820-d2f0214fea3b" href="https://academic.oup.com/journals/pages/authors/preparing_your_manuscript/research-data-policy#data2">More information and example statements</a></p>

<p>Authors may be asked to make available the underlying deidentified data on which their research relies to the Journal for inspection and verification during the peer review process.</p>

<h3>Data Citation</h3>

<p>The Journal supports the <a data-link-id="fca711a7-8981-4580-b50d-07c56dd9bbaf" href="https://force11.org/info/joint-declaration-of-data-citation-principles-final/">Force 11 Data Citation Principles</a> and requires that all publicly available datasets be fully referenced in the reference list with an accession number or unique identifier such as a digital object identifier (DOI). Data citations should include the minimum information recommended by <a data-link-id="59085069-7207-405e-8440-d4886d56f50e" href="http://www.datacite.org.s3-website-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/cite-your-data.html">DataCite</a>:</p>

<ul class="unbulleted">
	<li>[dataset] Authors, Year, Title, Publisher (repository or archive name), Identifier</li>
</ul>

<p>Authors should include the dataset tag – [dataset] – at the beginning of the citation. This helps the Publisher correctly identify and tag the citation. The tag will be removed from the citation published in the reference list.</p>

<h2><a data-link-id="254dd0af-63cb-4747-86c3-0dc51741a5d6" id="Preprints and self-archiving" name="Preprints and self-archiving"></a>Preprints and self-archiving</h2>

<h3>Author’s Original Version</h3>

<p><em>The Author’s Original Version (AOV) is defined here as the un-refereed author version of an article completed before submission of the article to the journal. This is sometimes referred to as the “preprint” version. The author accepts full responsibility for the article, and the content and layout are set out by the author. </em></p>

<p>Authors of all article types except ESC Guidelines may make their AOV available anywhere at any time. This includes posting on their own personal websites, institutional or non-commercial subject based repositories, commercial platforms websites or repositories, or social media, provided that, upon acceptance, they acknowledge that the article has been accepted for publication as follows:  </p>

<p>     This article has been accepted for publication in European Heart Journal, Published by Oxford University Press.  </p>

<p>After publication we would also ask authors to update their AOV with the Digital Object Identifier (DOI) and include a link to the Version of Record. </p>

<p><a data-link-id="e7431a9e-e81e-4138-a421-df67e8064367" href="https://academic.oup.com/pages/self_archiving_policy_b">More information about allowed channels and updating your preprint</a>.</p>

<p>Authors of preprints available in <a data-link-id="eaf9d42d-74c2-487f-8386-7b82dd57e89d" href="https://www.medrxiv.org/">medRxiv</a> or <a data-link-id="58074ff0-e1b5-46b5-94eb-6bb88b6c4a01" href="https://www.biorxiv.org/">bioRxiv</a> can submit their preprint directly from medRxiv or bioRxiv to <em>EHJ</em>. To do this, visit the Author Area of the preprint server website and select the Journal from the list of options. </p>

<p><a data-link-id="9483ca12-e692-4a8e-b23f-176be2d8dd63" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Submitting%20your%20medRxiv%20or%20bioRxiv%20preprint%20to%20EHJ">More information about submitting your preprint to <em>EHJ</em></a></p>

<h3>Accepted manuscript </h3>

<p><em>The accepted manuscript (AM) is the final draft author manuscript, as accepted for publication by a journal, including modifications based on referees’ suggestions, before it has undergone copyediting, typesetting and proof correction. This is sometimes referred to as the post-print version. </em></p>

<p>Immediately upon publication authors of all article types except ESC Guidelines may: </p>

<ul>
	<li>Immediately upload their AM to their own personal webpage (excluding commercial websites and repositories) </li>
	<li>Immediately upload their AM to their institutional or other non-commercial subject based repositories on the proviso that it is not made publicly available until after the specified embargo period </li>
</ul>

<p>After the embargo period of 12 months, authors of all article types except ESC Guidelines may upload their AM to institutional repository or other non-commercial repositories and make it publicly available. Accepted Manuscripts may not be uploaded or shared on commercial websites or repositories, unless the website or repository has signed a licensing agreement with OUP permitting such uploading or sharing.  </p>

<h3>Version of Record </h3>

<p><em>The Version of Record (VOR) is defined here as the final typeset and edited version of the journal article that has been made available by OUP by formally and exclusively declaring the article “published”. This includes any ‘advanced access’ article even before the compilation of a volume issue. </em></p>

<p>The VOR as it appears in the journal following copyediting and proof correction may not be deposited by authors in institutional repositories or posted to third party websites and made publicly available unless the article is published on an Open Access model licence that allows for such posting.  </p>

<h3><a data-link-id="54667206-325d-4ce5-b108-2f438e810894" id="Hypothesis Paper" name="Hypothesis Paper"></a>Hypothesis</h3>

<h4>Scope</h4>

<p>Articles proposing a novel or unconventional hypothesis that differs from current thinking in the field and is strongly supported by existing literature. The goal of these papers is to challenge the current way of considering the available evidence. The following five steps are suggested: 1) a description of the prevailing paradigm; 2) an explanation as to why the current way of thinking is deficient; 3) the presentation of a novel way of synthesizing the existing body of evidence.; 4) a summary of existing data that supports the new hypothesis; 5) a proposal of ways in which the new hypothesis can be tested.</p>

<p>Maximum word count: 1,500 (excluding the title, abstracts, legends, and references)</p>

<p>The Journal will consider submissions within its scope providing</p>

<ul>
	<li>it is the original work of the authors and does not duplicate any previously published work, including the work of the authors;</li>
	<li>it is not under consideration, in peer review, or accepted for publication in any journal other than <em>EHJ</em>;</li>
	<li>it has not been published in any other journal; and</li>
	<li>it contains nothing abusive, defamatory, libellous, obscene, fraudulent, or illegal.</li>
</ul>

<p>Authors should observe high ethical standards and obey publication best practices. The following are all unacceptable:</p>

<ul>
	<li>data falsification or fabrication</li>
	<li>plagiarism, including duplicate publication of the author’s own work without proper citation</li>
	<li>redundant publication</li>
	<li>misappropriation of work</li>
</ul>

<p>The Journal expects all authors to have read and understood the Journal’s <a data-link-id="b0bfe925-d9fc-4d8c-b897-9c535db4c64a" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Publication%20Ethics">Editorial Policies</a> and requirements for <a data-link-id="83f19b46-2cfa-4920-bfb3-28e31f94ea3e" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Ethical%20Reporting">Ethical Reporting</a> prior to submission.</p>

<h3>How to Submit</h3>

<p>Authors should submit their manuscript in <a data-link-id="4823c30f-7e0a-42d1-8014-bc66d3dfc2d5" href="https://www.editorialmanager.com/eurheartj/default2.aspx">Editorial Manager</a>. If the corresponding author has not previously submitted to the Journal, they will need to register for an account. <a data-link-id="f9316d6c-065f-4ec9-b3a1-16c8e5359bd7" href="https://www.editorialmanager.com/robohelp/16.1/index.htm#t=EM_Help.htm">More information</a>.</p>

<p>At initial submission authors are required to:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Answer all questions in the online submission form</li>
	<li>Provide a completed <a data-link-id="6429034a-e326-4517-b416-b280f578c00b" href="https://static.primary.prod.gcms.the-infra.com/static/site/eurheartj/document/ehj-declarations-form.docx?node=fa062d899ef89b868eb1">Declarations Form</a></li>
	<li>Submit all parts of the manuscript, including the abstract, figures, figure legends, and supplementary files</li>
</ul>

<p>Questions about the submission process can be sent to the Editorial Office at <a data-link-id="12149bea-a22c-4d8a-bfd7-5415ebece733" href="mailto:ehj@gemelli-isola.it">ehj@gemelli-isola.it</a>.</p>

<h3>Format Free Submission</h3>

<p>If preferred, authors may submit their manuscript without journal-specific formatting at initial submission.</p>

<p>Authors are still required to:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Answer all questions in the online submission form</li>
	<li>Provide a completed <a data-link-id="eb56f8ac-f402-4f81-a603-04eefad3c2cf" href="https://static.primary.prod.gcms.the-infra.com/static/site/eurheartj/document/ehj-declarations-form.docx?node=fa062d899ef89b868eb1">Declarations Form</a></li>
	<li>Submit all parts of the manuscript, including the abstract, figures, figure legends, and supplementary files. Figures may be embedded in the manuscript file or uploaded separately</li>
	<li>Include page numbers in the manuscript file</li>
</ul>

<p>If requested to submit a revised version of the manuscript, authors should refer to <a data-link-id="91162dd3-c245-41b8-8e23-f4d07814c3e2" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Manuscript%20Preparation">Manuscript Preparation</a> for formatting instructions and to <a data-link-id="0e43292f-4c46-4852-8901-54aadfd8dc66" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Submitting%20Revised%20Manuscripts">Submitting Revised Manuscripts</a>.</p>

<h3><a data-link-id="da5cf661-7f9a-4bdf-af08-5f606f0b712f" id="Submitting your medRxiv or bioRxiv preprint to EHJ" name="Submitting your medRxiv or bioRxiv preprint to EHJ"></a>Submitting your medRxiv or bioRxiv preprint to <em>EHJ</em></h3>

<p>Authors can save time in the submission process by submitting their medRxiv or bioRxiv preprint directly from the server to <em>EHJ</em>. To do this, visit the Author Area in medRxiv or bioRxiv and select <em>EHJ</em> from the list of options.</p>

<p>This process will transfer all manuscript files and author information to <em>EHJ</em>. You will then receive an email with a link to your submission in <em>EHJ</em>, where you will need to answer some additional questions and approve the manuscript for submission.</p>

<p>Authors submitting their preprint to <em>EHJ</em> should refer to the Journal’s <a data-link-id="02328ba2-8936-458d-ace8-97665aa5a371" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Preprints%20and%20self-archiving">Preprint Policy</a>. In particular, authors should note the following:</p>

<ul>
	<li>The preprint that you submit to<em> EHJ </em>must be the Author’s Original Version before any peer review.</li>
	<li>You cannot submit your preprint to more than one journal.</li>
	<li>If your paper is accepted for publication in <em>EHJ</em>, authors are responsible for updating the preprint with a DOI and the link to the published version of the article.</li>
</ul>

<h3><a data-link-id="ce5d4407-527b-43bd-87dc-21d7dfe42f2c" id="Submitting Revised Manuscripts" name="Submitting Revised Manuscripts"></a>Submitting Revised Manuscripts</h3>

<p>After peer review the submitting author may receive an email asking them to submit a revised version of their manuscript.</p>

<p>When submitting a revised manuscript, the submitting author should upload the following items to Editorial Manager:</p>

<ol>
	<li>A document containing responses to each of the points raised by the Editors and Reviewers. The document should clearly indicate what changes have been made to the manuscript. The document should be uploaded to the submission system with the document title “Letter Revised Manuscript” under the respective header.</li>
	<li>A revised final version of the manuscript, with all changes highlighted in yellow. The use of “track changes” is not recommended.</li>
</ol>

<p>Authors may also be asked to provide other items or information. This will be specified in the email to the submitting author.</p>

<h2><a data-link-id="fe2bf5a8-5416-47c2-9eb7-d8fb0821d099" id="Manuscript Preparation" name="Manuscript Preparation"></a>Manuscript Preparation</h2>

<h3>Pre-submission Language Editing</h3>

<p>Authors may choose to use a language-editing service before submitting to the Journal. A list of services is available on <a data-link-id="83085ffc-6b62-4538-9df8-f985e3854a16" href="https://academic.oup.com/pages/for-authors/journals/preparing-and-submitting-your-manuscript/language-services">OUP’s Language services page</a>. Language editing is optional and does not guarantee that the submission will be accepted. Edited manuscripts will still undergo peer review by the Journal according to the Journal’s <a data-link-id="0013913b-ba92-45e4-b7aa-bf1f91cf32b0" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Peer%20Review%20Policy">peer review policy</a>.</p>

<p>Oxford University Press partners with Enago, a leading provider of author services. Prospective authors of <em>EHJ</em> are entitled to a discount of 30% for editing services at Enago, via the <a data-link-id="bafe0cf8-f7fd-4976-ac0e-405ba8c85c6f" href="https://www.enago.com/pub/oup/">Specialist English Editing Services for Oxford University Press Authors page</a>.</p>

<h3>Style</h3>

<p>Oxford English spelling should be used throughout, except in quotations and in references.</p>

<h3>Abbreviations</h3>

<p>SI units of measurements should be used. Authors should define nonstandard abbreviations when they first appear in the manuscript.</p>

<h3>General Formatting</h3>

<p>Authors should follow the general guidance below:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Prepare the manuscript using a Word processing package (save in .doc format)</li>
	<li>Use double-spaced throughout the manuscript</li>
	<li>Number each page consecutively</li>
	<li>Include line numbers on all pages. Line numbers should restart on each page.</li>
	<li>Avoid using footnotes; use parentheses within brackets</li>
	<li>Type references in the correct order and style of the Journal (see <a data-link-id="5906f280-524f-4604-928f-14c563677a45" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#References">References</a> below)</li>
	<li>Type unjustified</li>
	<li>Do not use hyphenation except for compound words or terms</li>
	<li>Use the TAB key once to indent paragraphs</li>
	<li>Clearly identify uncommon symbols and any Greek letters.</li>
	<li>Use formatting in Word to indicate bold, italic, Greek, mathematics, superscript, and subscript characters</li>
	<li>Indicate the approximate position of each figure and table</li>
	<li>Write out numbers one to ten in full (e.g., ‘one’ not ‘1’) unless they are used as a unit of measurement or describe a figure, table, or video (e.g., Figure 1)</li>
</ul>

<h3>Structure</h3>

<p>Clinical Research Articles and Translational Science Articles should be structured as follows:</p>

<ol>
	<li>Title page</li>
	<li>Text abstract and keywords</li>
	<li>Structured graphical abstract or graphical abstract (see below)</li>
	<li>Translational perspective (for Translational Science Articles only)</li>
	<li>Introduction</li>
	<li>Methods</li>
	<li>Results</li>
	<li>Discussion</li>
	<li>Acknowledgements</li>
	<li>Funding</li>
	<li>Disclosure of interest</li>
	<li>Data availability statement</li>
	<li>References</li>
	<li>Figure legends</li>
	<li>Appendices</li>
</ol>

<p>The following should be uploaded as separate files to Editorial Manager:</p>

<ol>
	<li>Figures</li>
	<li>Tables</li>
	<li>Supplementary files</li>
</ol>

<p>There is no requirement to structure other article types according to a journal style, but the above should be used as a guide.</p>

<h3>Title Page</h3>

<p>The Title Page should include:</p>

<ul>
	<li>The full title of the paper</li>
	<li>All author names and affiliations</li>
	<li>The institution where the work was performed</li>
	<li>The mailing address and email address of one corresponding author</li>
</ul>

<p>An effective title describes the content and main messages of the manuscript clearly and succinctly. In general, article titles should:</p>

<ol>
	<li>be as short as possible</li>
	<li>include the most important keywords at the beginning</li>
	<li>avoid abbreviations or acronyms, unless the title will be very long without them</li>
</ol>

<h3>Abstracts</h3>

<p>Authors are required to provide a Text Abstract for most article types. Some article types also require a Structured Graphical Abstract or a Graphical Abstract. <a data-link-id="61d3034e-02f2-428b-89fc-1e30854b48be" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Article%20Types">What abstract is required for my article type?</a></p>

<h4>Text Abstract with headings:</h4>

<p>Required for: Clinical Research Article, Translational Science Article, Meta-analysis</p>

<p>Text Abstracts should not exceed 250 words and should not contain references. They should be submitted as a separate file in Editorial Manager at initial submission.</p>

<p>The Text Abstract should be structured using the following headings:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Background and Aims</li>
	<li>Methods</li>
	<li>Results</li>
	<li>Conclusions</li>
</ul>

<h4>Text Abstract without headings:</h4>

<p>Required for: State of the Art Review, Hypothesis, Great Debate, Special Article</p>

<p>Text Abstracts should not exceed 250 words and should not contain references or abbreviations. They should be submitted as a separate file in Editorial Manager at initial submission.</p>

<h4>Structured Graphical Abstract:</h4>

<p>Required for: Clinical Research Article, Translational Science Article, Meta-analysis</p>

<p>The Structured Graphical Abstract includes two parts: (1) text under three headings and (2) the graphic. Authors should submit the text element and the figure for the graphic element as separate files in Editorial Manager. If accepted for publication, the two elements will be professionally redrawn into a single Structured Graphical Abstract. The illustrators will work with the authors to discuss and develop the Structured Graphical Abstract before the manuscript is sent to the Publisher.</p>

<p><em>(1) Text element:</em></p>

<p>Authors should provide up to 40 words for each of the following headings:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Key Question</li>
	<li>Key Finding</li>
	<li>Take-home Message</li>
</ul>

<p>The text for the headings listed above should be supplied in a single editable file (e.g., .doc). The file should be uploaded to Editorial Manager with a clear document title (e.g., ‘structured graphical abstract text’).</p>

<p><em>(2) Graphic element:</em></p>

<p>The graphic should provide a visual summary of the aims, methods, and findings of the paper.</p>

<ul>
	<li>Size: 11.0 cm x 18.0 cm (height x width)</li>
	<li>Orientation: landscape</li>
	<li>Minimum resolution: 300 ppi (the ppi of an image can usually be found by right-clicking on an image file and selecting ‘Properties’)</li>
	<li>Font: use a sans serif font such as Myriad Pro, Arial, or Helvetica</li>
	<li>Font size: 10-12 points, and no smaller than 8 points</li>
	<li>File type: graphs should be provided as a vector file (e.g., .pdf, .ai, or .svg). Photographs to be included in the redrawn Structured Graphical Abstract should be provided as high resolution (300 ppi) bitmaps in .tiff format. All other image types should be provided in .tiff files where possible.</li>
	<li>Authors should provide a list of abbreviations, sorted alphabetically, if they are used in the graphic</li>
	<li>The figure legend may contain up to 80 words only</li>
	<li>If the quality is not sufficient the Editorial Office may contact the authors to ask for a replacement graphic</li>
</ul>

<p>Authors must obtain permission for any material being reproduced in the abstract, including images or tables, for which they are not the copyright holder. Permissions should be sought from the original copyright holder. <a data-link-id="ba35f8b1-dbd9-42f5-ac7f-646b877c4ba8" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Re-using%20Copyrighted%20Material">More information about re-using copyrighted material</a></p>

<p><a data-link-id="fe9aaf40-bdde-4549-be58-98f360fecf99" href="https://static.primary.prod.gcms.the-infra.com/static/site/eurheartj/document/Graphical-Abstract-Guidance.pdf?node=882c54d3204fdf39af79&version=2035213:6ff6158046dc25f9af83">Guidance on how to create a clear and engaging graphical abstract</a></p>

<p><a data-link-id="6a6df8c7-3403-4530-9882-03b821edf0c0" href="https://academic.oup.com/esc/pages/graphical-abstract-guide">A guide to graphical abstracts (infographic)</a></p>

<h4>Graphical Abstract:</h4>

<p>Required for: State of the Art Review, Editorial, Hypothesis, Viewpoint, Special Article</p>

<p>The Graphical Abstract should provide a visual summary of the main messages (take-home messages) of the paper.</p>

<ul>
	<li>Size: 11.00 cm x 18.0 cm (height x width)</li>
	<li>Orientation: landscape</li>
	<li>Minimum resolution: 300 ppi (the ppi of an image can usually be found by right-clicking on an image file and selecting ‘Properties’)</li>
	<li>Font: use a sans serif font such as Myriad Pro, Arial, or Helvetica</li>
	<li>Font size: text should be 10-12 points, and no smaller than 8 points</li>
	<li>Authors should provide a list of abbreviations, sorted alphabetically, if they are used in the graphic</li>
	<li>The figure legend may contain up to 80 words</li>
	<li>If the quality is not sufficient the Editorial Office may contact the authors to ask for a replacement graphic</li>
</ul>

<p>Authors must obtain permission for any material being reproduced in the abstract, including images or tables, for which they are not the copyright holder. Permissions should be sought from the original copyright holder. <a data-link-id="6ed8d9ed-87ea-407d-adfb-e082a318768c" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Re-using%20Copyrighted%20Material">More information about re-using copyrighted material</a></p>

<p><a data-link-id="acdd32c2-1c44-43a9-a7c4-aa4c7fcc0f7b" href="https://static.primary.prod.gcms.the-infra.com/static/site/eurheartj/document/Graphical-Abstract-Guidance.pdf?node=882c54d3204fdf39af79&version=2035213:6ff6158046dc25f9af83">Guidance on how to create a clear and engaging graphical abstract</a></p>

<p><a data-link-id="c2c99d80-6d0d-4c45-a457-a974eeb0d5c2" href="https://academic.oup.com/esc/pages/graphical-abstract-guide">A guide to graphical abstracts (infographic)</a></p>

<h4>Audio Abstract:</h4>

<p>Recommended for: Clinical Research Article, Translational Science Article, Meta-analysis, State of the Art Review, Hypothesis, Viewpoint</p>

<p>The Audio Abstract should provide an audio summary of the main messages (take-home messages) of the paper.</p>

<p>Authors should provide text for the Audio Abstract in a separate file, which should be uploaded under the ‘Audio Abstract’ header in Editorial Manager. If approved by the Editors, a professional speaker will record audio abstract for the paper using the text provided.</p>

<h4>Translational Perspective:</h4>

<p>Required for: Translational Science Article</p>

<p>The Translational Perspective should be a summary of relevant translational aspects for clinical applications. It should not exceed 100 words and should not contain any references or abbreviations.</p>

<h4>Summary:</h4>

<p>Authors should give an outline of the paper in a Summary, that will help the editorial team to evaluate and process the paper. Unlike abstracts, summaries are intended for internal use only and are not published alongside accepted articles.</p>

<h3>Keywords</h3>

<p>Authors should provide up to six keywords with the manuscript.</p>

<h3>Tables</h3>

<p>Formatting guidelines:</p>

<ul>
	<li>It is preferable to provide tables in portrait layout with no more than 9 columns</li>
	<li>Centre each column around its header</li>
	<li>Avoid using colour and shading, as these are not used when published.</li>
	<li>All tables should be numbered (e.g., Table 1) and referenced in the text.</li>
	<li>Tables should not be split into parts (e.g., Table 1a, 1b etc.).</li>
</ul>

<p>Submission guidelines:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Each table should be uploaded as a separate file in Editorial Manager.</li>
	<li>Tables should be in an editable format and should not be embedded as an image file.</li>
</ul>

<p>Please note that additional tables may be submitted as supplementary online-only material if permitted for the article type.</p>

<h3>Figures</h3>

<p>Figures should be limited to the number necessary for clarity and must not duplicate data from the tables or the text. Typically, submissions should have no more than eight figures and tables in total. Additional figures may be submitted as supplementary online-only material if permitted for the article type.</p>

<p>Figures should not be submitted if the copyright of the figure is unclear (e.g., images downloaded from the internet). Permission must be sought and granted for all figures being reproduced in the Journal.</p>

<p>Full attribution must be given for figures that have been generated by a third party or adapted or reproduced from a third party. Attribution must be given in the figure legend and in accordance with the licence of the original work.</p>

<p><a data-link-id="d7a8ca52-5f5d-4bfb-b24e-b02ea9237ea3" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Re-using%20Copyrighted%20Material">Find out more about permissions for the re-use of third-party material</a></p>

<h4>General guidance for all figure types:</h4>

<ul>
	<li>Each figure should be provided as an individual image file.</li>
	<li>Each figure should be numbered consecutively (e.g., Figure 1, Figure 2) and referenced in the text.</li>
	<li>Text in figures should use a sans serif font such as Myriad Pro, Arial, or Helvetica</li>
	<li>Note that the use of red and green in figures may cause difficulty for individuals with colour-blindness.</li>
	<li>Legends for figures should be included in a separate section of the manuscript grouped under the heading ‘Legends’, after the ‘References’ section. Define all symbols and abbreviations used in the figure. Common abbreviations and other in the preceding text should be not redefined in the legend.</li>
	<li><em>EHJ</em> does not charge for colour figures of any type.</li>
	<li>Guidance on file type, resolution, and quality for each type of figure is given below.</li>
</ul>

<h4>General guidance for all figure legends:</h4>

<ul>
	<li>Legends for figures should be included in a separate section at the end of the manuscript on a new page grouped under the heading ‘Figure Legends’.</li>
	<li>For each figure containing a graph, the legend should include the number of animals/cells/observations and the statistical test applied.</li>
	<li>It is preferable that authors provide the exact P-value in the figure legend (e.g., <em>P</em> = 0.003).</li>
	<li>Define all symbols and abbreviations used in the figure. Common abbreviations and other in the preceding text should be not redefined in the legend.</li>
</ul>

<h4>Photographs and Images:</h4>

<p>Photographs and images should be provided as raster images. Common examples of raster images are .tif/.tiff or .raw file types. The resolution of raster files is measured by the number of dots or pixels in a given area, referred to as “dpi” or “ppi”. This information is given in the image properties, which can usually be found by right-clicking on an image file and selecting ‘Properties’. Dpi and pixel width are included in the ‘Details’ tab.</p>

<ul>
	<li>Minimum resolution: 350 dpi</li>
	<li>Recommended resolution: 600 dpi</li>
	<li>It is not possible to improve the quality of an image during the production process. Before submitting a photograph or image check that details are clear, that contrast is good, and that there is low noise.</li>
</ul>

<h4>Line art:</h4>

<p>Line art images should be provided as raster images. Common examples of raster images are .tif/.tiff or .raw file types. The resolution of raster files is measured by the number of dots or pixels in a given area, referred to as “dpi” or “ppi”. This information is given in the image properties, which can usually be found by right-clicking on an image file and selecting ‘Properties’. Dpi and pixel width are included in the ‘Details’ tab.</p>

<ul>
	<li>Minimum resolution: 600 dpi</li>
	<li>Recommended resolution: 1200 dpi</li>
	<li>Colour: use CMYK or RGB format.</li>
	<li>Size: submit the line art in the size intended for publication in print</li>
	<li>Font: use a sans serif font such as Myriad Pro, Arial, or Helvetica</li>
	<li>Font size: no smaller than 2mm in height.</li>
	<li>If stippling is used, use clear black dots with visible white space between them. Faint and grey stippling will be lost during production and should be avoided.</li>
	<li>Ensure that it is easy to differentiate between different levels or types of shading.</li>
</ul>

<h4>Charts, graphs and diagrams:</h4>

<p>Charts, graphs, and diagrams are best rendered digitally as geometric forms called vector graphics. Common file types are .eps, .svg, .ai, and .pdf. Vector images use mathematical relationships between points and the lines connecting them to describe an image. These file types do not use pixels, which means that resolution does not apply to vector images.</p>

<ul>
	<li>It is preferable to use colour in charts, graphs, and diagrams rather than black and white or grayscale. Avoid pale colours and colour combinations that may be difficult for colour-blind readers.</li>
	<li>Ensure that it is easy to differentiate between different levels or types of shading.</li>
	<li>Colour should be submitted in CMYK or RGB format.</li>
	<li>Ensure that the axes are easy to read (i.e., clear tick marks and axes labels).</li>
	<li>Elements within diagrams should be clearly labelled and formatted consistently.</li>
</ul>

<h4>Multipanel figures:</h4>

<p>Submit all panels of a multipanel figure as a single file in Editorial Manager.</p>

<p>Preparation guidance:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Each panel should be labelled with a letter (e.g., A, B, C) in the upper-left corner.</li>
	<li>Multipanel figures should contain no more than 6 panels.</li>
	<li>Each panel of the multipanel figure should follow the guidance relevant to the figure type, given above. For example, a graph should refer to the guidance above for charts, graphs and diagrams.</li>
	<li>Dedicated software should be used to combine the panels into a single figure, such as Photoshop, GIMP, Illustrator, or InkScape. We do not recommend using PowerPoint.</li>
</ul>

<p></p><h4><a data-link-id="a14527cb-5c6c-44ba-8634-845a0cdfe02f" id="alt-text" name="alt-text"></a>Figure accessibility and alt text</h4>

<p>When submitting your manuscript, we require you to provide alt text (alternative text) descriptions for all images, figures, illustrations, and photographs included in the main article.  </p>

<p>Please consider accessibility when designing each figure, so that all images can be easily understood by visually impaired readers. OUP provides <a data-link-id="6e19d973-98cb-4e6d-8698-828d9aef4fcb" href="https://static.primary.prod.gcms.the-infra.com/static/umbrella/document/Figures_accessibility_journals_edition_v2.2_2024.pdf?node=aef6670590405d43ef10">detailed guidance on figure accessibility</a>, including contrast, text accessibility and alt text. It is also best practice for the information or data represented in the image to be fully described by the caption and/or surrounding text.</p>

<p>Please include each alt text description in your main manuscript file, directly under the figure legend for the relevant figure, preceded by ‘Alt text:’.  </p>

<p><a data-link-id="bd91f45a-ed95-4c8a-9daa-5489d3ca62f3" href="https://static.primary.prod.gcms.the-infra.com/static/site/journals/document/alt-text-figure-accessibility.pdf?node=1329505d4d63d87a12ed">Detailed guidance on how to draft and submit alt text</a>.   </p>

<p>Including alt text in your manuscript helps make your work more accessible to all readers. Good alt text ensures that individuals with visual impairments or those using screen readers can understand the content and context of your figures. The aim of alt text is to give concise and informative descriptions of your figures so all readers can understand and benefit from the visuals in your manuscript. Including alt text demonstrates a commitment to accessibility and enhances the overall impact and reach of your work.  </p>

<p>Alt text is only accessible via e-reader and will not appear as part of the typeset article.   </p>
<p></p>

<h3>Videos</h3>

<p>Formatting guidelines:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Format: .mp4 or .avi format only</li>
	<li>Videos should be numbered consecutively (e.g., Video 1, Video 2) and referenced in the text.</li>
	<li>Authors should provide a still image for each video, which will be used in the PDF version of the article. The video still should be provided in .eps, .svg, .ai, or .pdf format. Each video still should be clearly numbered (e.g., Video 1 still image, Video 2 still image).</li>
	<li>Please note that the Journal cannot use videos hosted on third-party sites such as YouTube, as the link may expire.</li>
</ul>

<p>Submission guidelines:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Upload each video and video still image as a separate file under the header “Video” in Editorial Manager.</li>
	<li>Legends for videos should be included in a separate section under the heading ‘Legends’, after the ‘References’ section of the manuscript. Define all symbols and abbreviation used in the video. Common abbreviations and other in the preceding text should be not redefined in the legend.</li>
	<li>Videos should not be submitted if the copyright of the video is unclear (e.g., a video downloaded from the internet). Permission must be sought and granted for all videos being reproduced in the Journal, and correct attribution must be given in accordance with the licence of the original work.</li>
	<li>Additional videos may be submitted as supplementary online-only material if permitted for the article type.</li>
</ul>

<h3>Acknowledgements</h3>

<p>Substantive contributions of individuals should be noted in an “Acknowledgements” section, above the “Conflict of Interest” section. This section can include individuals who do not meet the ICMJE criteria for authorship, but nevertheless were contributors to the paper. See the <a data-link-id="3adbab5c-f315-4ba2-afd9-3554e017a2be" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Authorship">Authorship</a> and <a data-link-id="7e2005c5-58c7-42f2-841b-380d15061c38" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Contributors">Contributors</a> sections above.</p>

<h3>Funding</h3>

<p>Details of all funding sources for the work should be given in a separate section entitled “Funding”. This should appear before the “Acknowledgements” section in the manuscript.</p>

<p>The following rules should be followed:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Funding agency names should be given in full without abbreviations: e.g., National Cancer Institute at the National Institutes of Health</li>
	<li>Grant numbers should be complete and accurate and provided in brackets: e.g., (grant number ABX CDXXXXXX)</li>
	<li>Multiple grant numbers should be separated by a comma: e.g. (grant numbers ABX CDXXXXXX, EFXXXXXX)</li>
	<li>Agencies should be separated by a semi-colon (plus ‘and’ before the last funding agency)</li>
	<li>Where individuals must be specified for certain sources of funding, the following text should be added after the relevant agency or grant number 'to [author initials]'.</li>
</ul>

<p>Funding statement examples:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Wellcome Trust (grant numbers AA-10101, BB949/2-3) to M.H. and P.P.F. Funding for open access charge: Wellcome Trust (grant number CB5453961-7).</li>
	<li>National Cancer Institute at the National Institutes of Health (grant number L-130-A); National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute at the National Institutes of Health (grant number A-158912/1); and National Institute of Nursing Research at the National Institutes of Health (grant numbers W-1120, G-819-1).</li>
</ul>

<h4>NIH-funded articles:</h4>

<p>OUP will deposit all NIH-funded articles in PubMed Central. Authors must ensure that manuscripts are clearly indicated as NIH-funded using the guidelines above.</p>

<h4>Crossref Funding Data Registry:</h4>

<p>To meet funding requirements, authors are required to name their funding sources, or state if there are none, during the submission process. For further information on this process or to find out more about CHORUS, visit the <a data-link-id="b3f78247-45ca-4a1b-b02c-66cf6fa95fcb" href="https://academic.oup.com/journals/pages/open_access/funder_policies/chorus">CHORUS initiative</a>.</p>

<h3><a data-link-id="9caa4ebb-718f-4500-8a56-ca0845962692" id="Group Authorship" name="Group Authorship"></a>Group Authorship</h3>

<p>When submitting a manuscript with a group author name:</p>

<ul>
	<li>The group author name should be given next to the authors, underneath the article title. For example:</li>
</ul>

<p>Cardiology in Europe</p>

<p>Lucie Tomková, Nimaat Shahid, Christian Onslow, …, Cardiology Task Force 2021</p>

<ul>
	<li>The group author name should not have a footnote or endnote, or any additional information in brackets after the name.</li>
	<li>Individuals in the group should be listed in a separate section at the end of manuscript called “Author Information”, above the “References” section.</li>
	<li>The group author name should be given exactly as it appears in the list of authors underneath the article title, followed by a colon and the list of names, each separated by a comma. For example:</li>
</ul>

<p>Author Information Cardiology Task Force 2021: Avelaine Brousseau, Naomi Castiglione, …</p>

<ul>
	<li>Affiliations or countries for the individuals in the group can be given in brackets, but superscript references must not be used. For example:</li>
</ul>

<p>Cardiology Task Force 2021: Avelaine Brousseau (France), Naomi Castiglione (Italy), …</p>

<h3><a data-link-id="752a0bc3-a691-4853-8de2-7a4a33669fe1" id="References" name="References"></a>References</h3>

<p>References should be identified in the text by Arabic numerals and numbered in the order cited. All references should be compiled at the end of the article in Vancouver style (i.e., author-number system). Complete information should be given for each reference, including the title of the article, abbreviated journal title, and page numbers. If there are more than six authors, the first six authors should be listed followed by ‘et al.’.</p>

<p>Personal communications, manuscripts in preparation, and other unpublished data should not be cited in the reference list but may be mentioned in parentheses in the text. Authors should obtain permission from the source to cite unpublished data. Titles of journals should be abbreviated in accordance with MEDLINE. If a journal is not listed in MEDLINE, the journal name should be written out in full.</p>

<p>Article citation examples:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Peters S, Reinders B. Cardiovascular Diseases. <em>Journal Abbrev</em> 2022;1:100–116. doi: https://doi.org/10.1093/journal/abc123</li>
	<li>Barbosa SA, Kulikova B, Lund R, Kowalska G, Burtole J, Ivanković SL, et al. <em>Cardiovascular Diseases. J Abbrev</em> 2022;10:15–20. doi: https://doi.org/10.1093/journal/def456</li>
</ul>

<p>Book citation example:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Nicholaus S, Ralla DE Jr. <em>Cardiovascular Diseases</em>. 4th ed. London: Publisher; 2021. p120-206.</li>
</ul>

<p>Chapter citation example:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Ryan D, Witteland AWR. Heart Failure. In: Nicholas S, Raffa DE. <em>Cardiovascular Diseases.</em> 4th ed. London: Publisher; 2021. p157–158.</li>
</ul>

<p>Conference proceedings example:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Brooks AD. Cardiology. In: <em>Abstracts of the Annual Conference</em>, Paris, France, 2022. Abstract A-2239, p671. International Society, Paris, France.</li>
</ul>

<p>Webpage citation example:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Cardiology Society. <em>Cardiovascular Diseases:</em> Summary. Available from: http://www. website.org (accessed 1 Jan 2022).</li>
</ul>

<p>Preprint article citation example:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Olsen T, Hughes C, Holmberg LB. Cardiovascular Diseases. <em>Biorxiv</em> [Preprint] 2022. Available from doi.org/10.0000/123456.</li>
</ul>

<p>The Journal’s style is available in <a data-link-id="1ec2fc15-34c9-44a7-8625-b38f4d44bd6d" href="https://endnote.com/style_download/european-heart-journal/">EndNote</a>.</p>

<h3>Supplementary Material</h3>

<p>For some article types, supporting material that is not essential for inclusion in the main text of the manuscript, but which would benefit the reader, can be made available online-only as supplementary material. Such information might include more detailed methods, extended data sets or data analysis, additional tables, figures, or videos.</p>

<p>Identifying information should not be published in written descriptions, photographs, or pedigrees unless the information is essential for scientific purposes and the patient (or parent or guardian) has given written informed consent for publication. <a data-link-id="3ee0311d-6b17-4ac1-9d11-492560661cfe" href="https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/pages/General_Instructions#Informed%20Patient%20Consent">More information about informed patient consent and the use of patient data</a></p>

<p>Authors must submit all supplementary material at the same time as the manuscript to be peer reviewed. The following guidance should be followed:</p>

<ul>
	<li>All supplementary material must be clearly labelled (e.g., Supplementary Figure 1, Supplementary Video 1 etc.)</li>
	<li>Supplementary material must be cited in the text of the main manuscript</li>
	<li>Style and formatting of supplementary material should be consistent with that of the manuscript and should be formatted to function on any internet browser. However, supplementary material will be not be copyedited or typeset and will be published online in the format provided during submission.</li>
	<li>The material should be uploaded in a non-editable format where possible</li>
	<li>It is not necessary to include the study protocol, but this could be referenced in the text if it is available online</li>
</ul>

<h2><a data-link-id="d0443761-c3b3-44ec-b28a-aa987eae022c" id="Embargoes and Press Releases" name="Embargoes and Press Releases"></a>Embargoes and Press Releases</h2>

<h3>Publication Embargoes</h3>

<p>The Journal will coordinate embargoes if this is required by the authors. Authors should email the Editorial Office (<a data-link-id="d4b19c6f-d6e6-42b8-aa57-b668a18d6753" href="mailto:ehj@gemelli-isola.it">ehj@gemelli-isola.it</a>) as soon as possible if an embargo is required, stating the exact date and time that the paper can be published. Authors should include a note in the cover letter at submission and when returning proofs.</p>

<h3>Press Releases</h3>

<p>If a press release will be prepared and issued by the institution or funder of one or more of the authors, the authors should reach out to the <em>EHJ</em> Editorial Office (<a data-link-id="90f8e6f2-b71d-4f2f-94ad-b2a9a60aac39" href="mailto:ehj@gemelli-isola.it">ehj@gemelli-isola.it</a>) as soon as possible and before a final decision is made on the article.</p>

<p>If the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) or OUP on behalf of the Journal opt to take forward a press release, the authors will be contacted by <a data-link-id="cebdb1b2-0a20-4678-9490-34c3b8313783" href="mailto:press@escardio.org">press@escardio.org</a>.</p>

<h2><a data-link-id="75fd2b31-3168-4b81-8f11-bc6d41420c6f" id="Publication Agreements and Open Access" name="Publication Agreements and Open Access"></a>Publication Agreements and Open Access</h2>

<p><em>EHJ</em> offers authors the option of publishing under a standard licence or an open access licence. Some funders require open access publication as a condition of funding. Authors should clarify any requirements with their funder or institution as soon as possible.</p>

<p>In signing a standard licence to publish the corresponding author (on behalf of all authors) grants an exclusive licence to the European Society of Cardiology to publish their paper in <em>EHJ</em>. There is no charge to publish under a standard licence.</p>

<p>If publishing open access, authors will need to pay an open access charge. Please note that if you have been invited to submit to the Journal, and you select an open access licence, you will still be required to pay. <a data-link-id="c1365862-d7c3-4f65-8cdd-18c4da0c47ad" href="https://academic.oup.com/journals/pages/open_access/charges">Details of open access licences and charges</a>.</p>

<p>OUP has a growing number of Read and Publish agreements with institutions and consortia which provide funding for open access publishing. This means that authors from participating institutions can publish open access, and the institution will pay the charge. <a data-link-id="1c4a5f5b-035b-4b74-94c5-946da7d47016" href="https://academic.oup.com/journals/pages/authors/production_and_publication/publication-charges/read-and-publish-agreements/participating-journals-and-institutions">Find out if your institution is participating and whether your paper is eligible</a>.</p>

<p>To be eligible for one of OUP’s Read and Publish agreements, the corresponding author must provide their qualifying institution as their primary affiliation when they submit their manuscript. After submission, changing the corresponding author in order to access Read and Publish funding is not permissible.</p>

<h2><a data-link-id="9a3ba23b-14d2-47fd-a3ad-5b09f7ab8db7" id="Publication process" name="Publication process"></a>Publication process</h2>

<p>Page proofs will be submitted to the corresponding author electronically. These should be checked thoroughly for any changes or typographic errors.</p>

<p>It is the Publisher’s intent to review and correct the proofs and publish the accepted work as soon as possible. To achieve this, all corrections must be returned to the Publisher within 3 days. Corrections must be returned to the Publisher within 1 day for Fast Tracks.</p>

<h2><a data-link-id="6d5e46d5-6bfb-47e5-a237-a744ef10bf46" id="Post-publication changes" name="Post-publication changes"></a>Post-publication changes</h2>

<h3>Corrections</h3>

<p>The Journal will only make changes to published papers if the publication record is seriously affected by the academic accuracy of the published information.</p>

<p>Changes to published papers are accompanied by a formal correction notice. This applies to papers on Advance Access and those published within an issue. This means that any change carried out to a paper already published online will have a corresponding correction published with its own DOI. The notice will be published online at the earliest opportunity (on the Journal’s Advance Articles page if possible, otherwise in the earliest available issue), and will link to the paper being corrected. A link will also appear on the paper being corrected, notifying readers that a correction has been published.</p>

<p>Changes cannot be made to papers that have been published online for more than 12 months. In such instances a correction will be published explaining the error, but the paper will not be updated. The correction will be published online with links to the original paper as described above.</p>

<p>For more information and details of how to request changes, including for authors who wish to update their name and/or pronouns, please see OUP’s policy on <a data-link-id="819c15a8-5a87-4823-8643-f11a2e2c7d73" href="https://academic.oup.com/pages/for-authors/journals/final-steps-to-publication/changes-to-published-articles">changes to published papers</a>. </p>

<h3>Retractions</h3>

<p>The Journal subscribes to the <a data-link-id="3739c97e-8650-4c03-83bc-5dbdb0a54f19" href="https://publicationethics.org/guidance/guideline/retraction-guidelines">COPE Retraction Guidelines</a>, which outlines appropriate use cases for retractions. The Journal also has the option of consulting the ESC Journal Publications Ethics Committee.</p>

<h2><a data-link-id="501a8b68-40b2-48b2-9268-a5c36fb1c356" id="Contact the Journal" name="Contact the Journal"></a>Contact the Journal</h2>

<p>For any questions or feedback please contact <a data-link-id="c8311511-3b68-4e66-9764-70c0ee1f7816" href="mailto:ehj@gemelli-isola.it">ehj@gemelli-isola.it</a>.</p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          <div class="journal-paragraph" style="border-bottom: 4px solid #e61938;" id="about">

              <h2>About</h2>
              <div class="detail-about-para"><p style="margin-bottom:11px">The <em>Journal of the London Mathematical Society</em> has been publishing leading research across a broad range of mathematics since 1926.</p>

<p>Articles published in the <em>Journal of the London Mathematical Society</em> represent a significant advance in mathematical knowledge, or are deemed to stimulate new interest and research activity. The articles have a minimum length of 18 pages and no maximum length.</p>

<p>The <em>Journal of the London Mathematical Society </em>shares an <a href="https://www.lms.ac.uk/publications/BJ-Editorial-Board">Editorial Board</a> with the <a href="https://www.lms.ac.uk/publications/blms"><i>Bulletin </i><em>of the London Mathematical Society</em></a>. The <em>Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society </em>publishes concise research articles (20 pages and below). Both journals employ the same high standard of peer review.</p>
</div>
                          </div>
                                                                      <div class="journal-paragraph" style="" id="publications-managed-by-mathematicians-for-mathematicians">

              <h2>Publications managed by mathematicians for mathematicians</h2>
              <div class="detail-about-para"><p>The <i>Journal of the London Mathematical Society </i>is<i> </i>wholly owned and managed by the London Mathematical Society as one of its charitable activities.</p>

<p>100% of the Society's publishing profits are reinvested in mathematics, supporting mathematicians and mathematics research in the form of research grants, conference grants, prizes, initiatives for early career researchers, and the promotion of mathematics.</p>

<p>Publishing your research in the <i>Journal of the London Mathematical Society </i>directly supports the charitable work of the Society.</p>
</div>
                          </div>
                                                                      <div class="journal-paragraph" style="" id="submitting-to-the-journal">

              <h2>Submitting to the Journal</h2>
              <div class="detail-about-para"><p>Before submitting an article to the <em>Journal of the London Mathematical Society</em>, we recommend that authors read the <strong><a href="https://www.lms.ac.uk/publications/jlms/submission">submission guidelines for the <em>Journal</em></a></strong>.</p>

<p>All articles published in this journal are peer reviewed. Editors may reject papers without external review. Read our <strong><a href="https://www.lms.ac.uk/publications/jlms/peerreview">full peer review policy</a></strong>.</p>

<p>If a paper is accepted for publication in the <em>Journal of the London Mathematical Society, </em>it will be sent to the publisher for typesetting. Find out more about <strong><a href="https://www.lms.ac.uk/publications/jlms/accepted">what happens to an article after it is accepted</a></strong>.</p>
</div>
                          </div>
                                                                      <div class="journal-paragraph" style="" id="related-publications">

              <h2>Related publications</h2>
              <div class="detail-about-para"><p style="margin-bottom:11px">The London Mathematical Society also publishes other peer-reviewed journals.</p>

<ul>
	<li>The <a href="https://www.lms.ac.uk/publications/plms"><em>Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society</em> </a>is the Society’s flagship, high-impact publication. The <em>Proceedings </em>publishes articles of the highest quality and significance across a broad range of mathematics, and the articles are of general interest to mathematicians.</li>
	<li>The <em><a href="https://www.lms.ac.uk/publications/blms">Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society</a></em> is the sister publication of the <em>Journal of the London Mathematical Society</em> and focuses on the publication of concise articles reporting significant advances in mathematical knowledge, as well as survey articles and obituaries.</li>
	<li>The <a href="https://lms.ac.uk/publications/tlms"><em>Transactions of the London Mathematical Society</em></a> is a fully open access journal which publishes articles across the full range of mathematics.</li>
	<li>The <em><a href="https://www.lms.ac.uk/publications/jtop">Journal of Topology</a> </em>is dedicated to articles of high quality and significance in topology, geometry and adjacent areas of mathematics.</li>
</ul>
</div>
                          </div>
                                                                      <div class="journal-paragraph" style="" id="open-access">

              <h2>Open Access</h2>
              <div class="detail-about-para"><p>The <em>Journal of the London Mathematical Society</em> is a hybrid open access journal. By default, articles in the journal will be published on a subscription basis and only be accessible to journal subscribers. The journal has options for gold and green open access publication.</p>

<p>Before submitting to the <em>Journal of the London Mathematical Society</em>, authors should <a href="https://authorservices.wiley.com/author-resources/Journal-Authors/licensing-open-access/open-access/author-compliance-tool.html" target="_blank">check any open access requirements from their institution or funder</a>.</p>

<p>If you are required to publish on an open access basis but you cannot identify a compliant route with <em>Journal of the London Mathematical Society</em>, please <a href="mailto:lmsjournals@lms.ac.uk">contact the journal team</a> before submitting.</p>

<p>See our <a href="https://www.lms.ac.uk/publications/open-access">open access page</a> for more information.</p>
</div>
                          </div>
                                                                      <div class="journal-paragraph" style="" id="subscribe">

              <h2>Subscribe</h2>
              <div class="detail-about-para"><p><a href="http://ordering.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/subs.asp?ref=1460-244X&doi=10.1112/(ISSN)1460-244X" target="_blank">Contact the publisher</a> to subscribe to this journal or renew your current subscription.</p>

<p>Members of the London Mathematical Society can receive free online access to the following publications if they have signed up for free online access via their LMS membership record.</p>

<ul>
	<li><em><a href="https://www.lms.ac.uk/publications/blms">Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society</a></em></li>
	<li><em><a href="https://www.lms.ac.uk/publications/jlms">Journal of the London Mathematical Society</a></em></li>
	<li><em><a href="https://www.lms.ac.uk/publications/plms">Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society</a></em></li>
</ul>

<p><br>
Free online access to these three journals can be activated via the LMS Membership Profile here: <a href="http://www.lms.ac.uk/user">www.lms.ac.uk/user</a> and selecting the preferred journals under the “My LMS Membership” tab.</p>

<p>The LMS will then notify Wiley, who will issue members with a username and password to log in to the <a href="https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/">Wiley Online Library</a>.</p>
</div>
                          </div>
                                                                      <div class="journal-paragraph" style="" id="contact">

              <h2>Contact</h2>
              <div class="detail-about-para"><h4>Submissions</h4>

<p>For any queries about submitting to the journal, articles under review, the peer review process or the submission system, contact the LMS team: <a href="mailto:lmsjournals@lms.ac.uk">lmsjournals@lms.ac.uk</a></p>

<h4>Accepted articles</h4>

<p>For accepted articles which have not been passed to the publisher for production, contact the LMS team: <a href="mailto:production@lms.ac.uk">production@lms.ac.uk</a></p>

<p>For accepted articles which have been passed to Wiley for production, contact the Wiley team: <a href="mailto:jlms@wiley.com">jlms@wiley.com</a></p>

<h4>Rights and permissions</h4>

<p>Find information on <a href="https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/permissions">the Wiley website</a>.</p>

<h4>All other enquiries</h4>

<p>Contact the LMS team: <a href="mailto:lmsjournals@lms.ac.uk">lmsjournals@lms.ac.uk</a></p>
</div>
